content.content:
# so a runtime guard at the first executable line runs first and never reaches
# them). If a bash >=4 exists (the framework already requires it — beads-health
# etc. source bash-version-guard.sh), re-exec under it; stdin (the hook payload)
# and argv survive exec. Otherwise FAIL CLOSED (exit 2 = block): a
# destructive-command fence must never silently allow when it cannot evaluate.
# The generic bash-version-guard.sh exits 1, which is a NON-blocking PreToolUse
# hook error (fail-OPEN) — wrong direction for this hook, hence the inline form.
if [ "${BASH_VERSINFO:-0}" -lt 4 ]; then
    for _bh_cand in /opt/homebrew/bin/bash /usr/local/bin/bash /usr/bin/bash bash; do
        if command -v "$_bh_cand" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            _bh_major="$("$_bh_cand" -c 'echo "${BASH_VERSINFO:-0}"' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
            if [ "${_bh_major:-0}" -ge 4 ]; then exec "$_bh_cand" "$0" "$@"; fi
        fi
    done
    echo "[block-destructive-bash] BLOCKED: bash >=4 required to evaluate the destructive-command fence (found ${BASH_VERSION:-unknown}); refusing to run degraded rather than allow a command unchecked. Install bash>=4 (macOS: brew install bash)." >&2
    exit 2
fi

if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if [[ -z "${LOA_BLOCK_DESTRUCTIVE_JQ_MISSING_WARNED:-}" ]]; then
    echo "WARNING: block-destructive-bash: jq not in PATH — destructive-command pattern matching is DISABLED for this session. Install jq to restore safety guards." >&2
    export LOA_BLOCK_DESTRUCTIVE_JQ_MISSING_WARNED=1
  fi
  exit 0  # Existing fail-open behavior preserved.
fi

# perf pass-2: pin byte-oriented ASCII regex/case-fold semantics for both the
# remaining greps and the bash [[ =~ ]]/${var,,} conversions. All patterns in
# this file are pure-ASCII; C-locale folding is the semantics they were
# written for (and what the test/golden harness already pins).
export LC_ALL=C

# Read tool input from stdin (JSON with tool_input.command).
# Path A jq call (SDD §6.4): failure here → empty $command → allow.
# perf pass-2: jq reads the hook's stdin directly — identical bytes reach the
# same jq program; the interim $(cat) copy and echo-pipe only added 2 forks.
command=$(jq -r '.tool_input.command // empty' 2>/dev/null) || true

# If we can't parse the command, allow (don't block on parse errors).
if [[ -z "$command" ]]; then
  exit 0
fi

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# quote-blindness scrub (bd-bdb-quote-blindness-pt1g).
# Produce _cmd_match, a LOCAL scrub-copy of $command used SOLELY for the
# block/allow decision below. $command itself is left byte-for-byte intact so
# emit_block's audit row still records the operator's original command.
#
# The fence is quote-blind: it sees a destructive TOKEN (rm -rf, DROP/TRUNCATE
# TABLE, DELETE FROM, git branch -D, ...) inside an INERT data carrier — an
# echo argument, a git commit message, a bead description, a gh PR body — and
# blocks a harmless command. The GENERAL problem (deciding whether an arbitrary
# quoted string will be executed) is NOT tractable in a regex fence — any
# allowlist of *execution* shapes (ssh/su -c/sh -c/xargs/...) is unbounded and
# reintroduces bypass (issue #1047). This is the INVERSE: a curated allowlist
# of KNOWN-INERT data carriers, whose value we redact into the scrub-copy.
#
# The metadata content gate (cycle-120 C-D3a) leaves values containing `$(` or
# backticks INTACT, including `$$(...)`. Those expansions can execute even in
# double quotes. A lone `$` is permitted. Double-quote escapes are consumed as
# pairs so an escaped quote cannot open a fake tail flag spanning a live write.
# The command-position prefix check rejects names inside other quoted data or
# interpreter/eval arguments. Unknown contexts retain conservative matching;
# these bounded recognizers do not establish arbitrary execution semantics.
#
# Carrier values may contain literal separators; following executable segments
# remain visible, so `echo 'safe' && rm -rf /` still blocks. Word boundaries and
# the prefix check keep `notgit commit -m '…'` from matching. echo/printf stays a sed
# scrub (rest-of-segment, not a quoted value); the git/br/gh quoted-value
# carriers use the content-gated bash loop `_bdb_scrub` below (replace the value
# with a single SPACE, never empty). BSD/GNU ERE only — no \b (BSD libc lacks
# it; header §).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Bare echo/printf carrier: from a segment-start echo/printf to the end of its
# segment. The rest-class excludes ; & | (segment separators — per-segment
# scoping), $ and backtick (command-substitution — never redact past them), and
# < > (redirect operators — leave redirects + their targets intact so the FR-SZ
# State-Zone write guard, which keys off the raw path, still fires on
# `echo x >> .run/cron.d/job.sh`).
_bdb_sed_echo='s/(^|;|&&|\|\||\|)([[:space:]]*(sudo[[:space:]]+)?(echo|printf)[[:space:]]+)[^;&|<>$`]*/\1\2 /g'

     5	#
     6	# The surgical-diff hook keys its running total on the checkpoint task
     7	# (`run-checkpoint.sh read --json`), else the sprint, else the session id;
     8	# keeps one sanitised file per task under the state directory (at most 20);
     9	# deletes the legacy session-long file; writes the summary the review's
    10	# SURGICAL axis reads; and is silent when the knob is off. A fixture
    11	# checkpoint (LOA_RUN_DIR) and a fake `br` on PATH stand in for a live run.
    12	# =============================================================================

    18	    HOOK="$R/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh"
    19	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not available"
    20	    command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not available"
    21	    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"

    37	# checkpoint <sprint> [task] — a schema-2 run state with that checkpoint
    38	checkpoint() {

    40	        '{schema_version: 2, state: "RUNNING",

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# run-checkpoint.sh — run position in .run/ (cycle-125 FR-3, SDD D-3.2;
# cycle-129 FR-4(f)/FR-5, SDD D-4.6, D-5.1 … D-5.4). Beads are the task ledger;
# the checkpoint is a HINT; the run state and the breaker are caches DERIVED
# from files (COMPLETED markers, LOA-VERDICT trailers, the ledger, git).
#
#   run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint sprint-N --phase PHASE [--task BEAD-ID] [--file F]
#       Atomically sets .schema_version = 2, .checkpoint = {sprint, task, phase, ts}
#       and .timestamps.last_activity = ts: jq → F.tmp.$$ → mv -f, under flock
#       on F.lock. F must already exist (a run in progress). Then runs
#       `derive --write` (a missing ledger is skipped). Exit 0 · 2 usage /
#       no run · 3 write failed (the previous file is untouched).
#   run-checkpoint.sh read [--file F] [--json]
#       Prints the checkpoint when it is trustworthy: parses, and when a task
#       is named, `br show <task> --json` reports it closed (a checkpoint that
#       names an open or unknown bead is DISCARDED with a logged line — beads
#       remain the recovery source). schema_version 1 / no checkpoint → prints
#       "sprint granularity". Exit 0 always when F exists; 2 when it does not.
#   run-checkpoint.sh derive [--json] [--write] [--root DIR] [--file F]
#       For the ledger's active cycle, per sprint: global_id, local_label,
#       ledger status, completed_marker (a2a/sprint-<gid>/COMPLETED exists and
#       the feedback trailers name this sprint, as sprint-<gid> or the local
#       label; a trailer or a `sprint:` line naming another sprint makes it a
#       stale_marker, treated as absent), review/audit verdicts (verdict-derive.sh;
#       APPROVED needs exit 0; a file without a trailer is legacy: no verdict,
#       listed in derivation.legacy_feedback), impl_commit (newest non-merge
#       commit on HEAD since max(sprint started|created, cycle created) touching
#       a path outside grimoires/, .run/, REPO-MAP.md, checksums.json,
#       CHANGELOG.md) and state complete | awaiting_marker | in_progress.
#       Run state, first match wins:
#         cache .state or .status JACKED_OUT, or .completion.merged_sha → JACKED_OUT (terminal)
#         breaker OPEN, or cache HALTED                                 → HALTED (sticky until /run-resume)
#         every sprint complete                                         → COMPLETE
#         cache COMPLETE and the ledger registers no new incomplete sprint → COMPLETE
#         last_activity within run_mode.stale_hours (12)                → RUNNING
#         otherwise                                                     → INTERRUPTED
#       Breaker (active sprint = first incomplete, else the last): the ordered
#       rounds engineer-feedback-r*.md, auditor-sprint-feedback-r*.md and the
#       current files (sorted by trailer ts, round, gate; rounds before the
#       breaker's reset_at are ignored) give cycle_count (non-APPROVED rounds),
#       same_issue (consecutive equal hashes) and no_progress (consecutive
#       equal counts); each cached counter is raised to its recomputed value,
#       never lowered; OPEN when a count threshold is met (timeout is left to
#       record-round). --json prints the derivation; --write rewrites F
#       (.state canonical, .status mirrored, derived_at, derivation {source,
#       stale_markers, legacy_feedback, sprint_ids}; schema_version kept) and
#       the breaker, under their locks — only when F exists, parses, and
#       run_mode.file_authoritative is not false (false = report-only).
#       Exit 0 · 4 no ledger / no active cycle · 2 usage.
#   run-checkpoint.sh record-round --gate review|audit --file FEEDBACK [--sprint sprint-N]
#                                  [--state-file F] [--breaker B]
#       After a review or audit: verdict-derive.sh --json on FEEDBACK; the
#       same-issue hash is md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` of that output
#       (no trailer: md5 of the first 50 lines from ## Findings / ## Issues /
#       ## Changes Required). APPROVED (exit 0) leaves every counter as is.
#       Otherwise, atomically on B: same_issue +1 when the hash equals
#       last_hash, else count 1 and last_hash = hash; no_progress +1 when the
#       counts equal the previous round's, else 0; cycle_count.current +1; then
#       the triggers in order same_issue ≥ threshold, no_progress ≥ threshold,
#       cycle_count ≥ limit, timeout (now - started ≥ limit_hours). A trip sets
#       state OPEN, appends history {timestamp, trigger, reason, gate, sprint},
#       sets F (.run/state.json) .state = HALTED, prints
#       `TRIPPED: <trigger>: <reason>` and exits 10 (also when B is already OPEN).
#       Exit 0 recorded · 2 usage / missing file · 3 write failed · 10 tripped.
#   run-checkpoint.sh mark --skill implement|bug --sprint ID [--root DIR]
#       Writes .run/implement-active.json {skill, sprint, started_at} (the
#       implement gate's marker sanction, valid two hours), then runs
#       `derive --write` when F exists. `unmark` removes the marker. Exit 0 · 2 usage.
#
# Default F: $LOA_RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json, else <root>/.run/sprint-plan-state.json
# (--root DIR sets <root> and ignores LOA_RUN_DIR). B: <run dir>/circuit-breaker.json.
# Readers accept schema_version 1 and 2 and files without derived_at/derivation.
# Config (<root>/.loa.config.yaml, yq; absent = defaults): run_mode.stale_hours (12),
# run_mode.file_authoritative (true), run_mode.circuit_breaker.{same_issue,no_progress}_threshold
# (3, 5), run_mode.defaults.{max_cycles,timeout_hours} (20, 8) for a new breaker file.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
VERDICT_DERIVE="$SCRIPT_DIR/verdict-derive.sh"
usage() { sed -n '3,/^# Default F/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2; }

sub="${1:-}"; [[ -n "$sub" ]] || usage; shift
file="" sprint="" task="" phase="" json=0 write=0 root="" gate="" state_file="" breaker="" skill=""
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --file)   [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --sprint) [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || usage; sprint="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --task)   [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || usage; task="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --phase)  [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Z_]+$ ]] || usage; phase="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --json)   json=1; shift ;;
    --write)  write=1; shift ;;
    --root)   [[ $# -ge 2 && -d "${2:-}" ]] || usage; root="$(cd "$2" && pwd)"; shift 2 ;;
    --gate)   [[ $# -ge 2 && ( "$2" == review || "$2" == audit ) ]] || usage; gate="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --state-file|--file-state) [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; state_file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --breaker) [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; breaker="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --skill)  [[ $# -ge 2 && ( "$2" == implement || "$2" == bug ) ]] || usage; skill="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    *) usage ;;
  esac
done

# Root and run dir: --root wins (and pins the run dir under it); else the
# directory holding a --file that sits in a .run/ dir (write/read/derive only);
# else this script's checkout with $LOA_RUN_DIR honoured.
if [[ -n "$root" ]]; then
  run_dir="$root/.run"
else
  root="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  run_dir="${LOA_RUN_DIR:-$root/.run}"
  if [[ -n "$file" && "$sub" != record-round ]]; then
    fdir="$(cd "$(dirname "$file")" 2>/dev/null && pwd)" || fdir=""
    if [[ -n "$fdir" && "$(basename "$fdir")" == .run ]]; then root="$(dirname "$fdir")"; run_dir="$fdir"; fi
  fi
fi
if [[ "$sub" != record-round && -z "$file" ]]; then file="$run_dir/sprint-plan-state.json"; fi
[[ -n "$breaker" ]] || breaker="$run_dir/circuit-breaker.json"
[[ -n "$state_file" ]] || state_file="$run_dir/state.json"

content.content:
now_iso() { date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ; }

# cfg KEY → the raw yq value ("null" when absent or unreadable). yq's `//`
# treats false as absent, so callers compare the raw text.
cfg() {
  local v
  if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -f "$CONFIG" ]]; then
    v=$(yq "$1" "$CONFIG" 2>/dev/null) || v="null"
    printf '%s' "${v//\"/}"
  else
    printf 'null'
  fi
}
cfg_int() {  # KEY DEFAULT MAX → a positive integer ≤ MAX, else DEFAULT
  local v; v=$(cfg "$1")
  if [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( v > 0 && v <= $3 )); then printf '%s' "$v"; else printf '%s' "$2"; fi
}

_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }

# atomic_update FILE JQ-ARGS... — jq over FILE (or {} when FILE is absent) →
# FILE.tmp.$$ → mv -f, under flock on FILE.lock. Exit 3 on any failure; the
# previous file is untouched.
atomic_update() {
  local f="$1"; shift
  local tmp="$f.tmp.$$" rc=0
  (
    # flock is util-linux (Linux); without it (macOS) the write is still atomic
    # (tmp + mv) but concurrent writers may interleave — last writer wins.
    if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then flock -w 5 9 || { echo "run-checkpoint: lock timeout on $f.lock" >&2; exit 3; }; fi
    if [[ -f "$f" ]]; then
      jq "$@" "$f" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: $f is not valid JSON — not written" >&2; exit 3; }
    else
      jq "$@" <<<'{}' > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: could not build $f" >&2; exit 3; }
    fi
    jq -e . "$tmp" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: refusing to replace $f with unparseable output" >&2; exit 3; }
    mv -f -- "$tmp" "$f"
  ) 9>"$f.lock" || rc=$?
  return $rc
}

cmd_write() {
  [[ -n "$sprint" && -n "$phase" ]] || usage
  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: no run state at $file (start a run first)" >&2; return 2; fi
  local ts rc=0
  ts=$(now_iso)
  atomic_update "$file" --arg s "$sprint" --arg t "$task" --arg p "$phase" --arg ts "$ts" \
    '.schema_version = 2
     | .checkpoint = {sprint: $s, task: (if $t == "" then null else $t end), phase: $p, ts: $ts}
     | .timestamps = ((.timestamps // {}) + {last_activity: $ts})' || rc=$?
  (( rc == 0 )) || return $rc
  # Every checkpoint refreshes the derived caches (D-5.2); a missing ledger (4) is not an error here
  local err drc=0
  err=$( { write=1; json=0; cmd_derive >/dev/null; } 2>&1 ) || drc=$?
  if (( drc != 0 && drc != 4 )); then printf '%s\n' "$err" >&2; fi
  return 0
}

bead_closed() {  # $1 bead id → 0 when br reports closed
  command -v br >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 2
  local js st
  js=$(br show "$1" --json 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  st=$(printf '%s' "$js" | jq -r 'if type=="array" then .[0] else . end | .status // .issue.status // empty' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  [[ "$st" == "closed" ]]
}

cmd_read() {
  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: no run state at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
  if ! jq -e . "$file" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "run-checkpoint: $file unparseable — no checkpoint; beads are the recovery truth" >&2; if (( json )); then echo '{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"unparseable"}'; fi; return 0; fi
  local sv cp s t p ts reason="" brc
  sv=$(jq -r '.schema_version // 1' "$file"); cp=$(jq -c '.checkpoint // null' "$file")
  [[ "$sv" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || sv=1
  if [[ "$cp" == "null" || "$sv" -lt 2 ]]; then
    if (( json )); then echo '{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"sprint granularity"}'; else echo "checkpoint: none (schema_version $sv → sprint granularity; resume at the first open bead of sprints.current)"; fi
    return 0
  fi
  s=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.sprint // empty' "$file"); t=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.task // empty' "$file"); p=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.phase // empty' "$file"); ts=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.ts // empty' "$file")
  if [[ -z "$s" || -z "$p" ]]; then reason="malformed checkpoint"
  elif [[ -n "$t" ]]; then
    # A task checkpoint is trusted only when beads CONFIRMS the task closed;
    # "br unavailable" is not a confirmation (Bridgebuilder PR #1269 FIND-003).
    brc=0; bead_closed "$t" || brc=$?
    case $brc in 0) ;; 2) reason="beads unavailable — task $t cannot be verified";; *) reason="task $t is not closed in beads";; esac
  fi
  if [[ -n "$reason" ]]; then
    echo "run-checkpoint: discarding checkpoint ($reason) — resume from the first open bead of $s" >&2
    if (( json )); then jq -cn --arg r "$reason" --arg s "$s" '{checkpoint:null, reason:$r, sprint:$s}'; else echo "checkpoint: discarded ($reason); resume at the first open bead of $s"; fi
    return 0
  fi
  if (( json )); then jq -c '{checkpoint: .checkpoint}' "$file"
  else echo "checkpoint: $s ${t:+task $t }phase $p at $ts → resume at the first open bead after $t in $s"; fi
}

# fb_parse FILE GATE → one compact JSON object: {file, exists, trailer, verdict,
# counts, exit_code, sprint_id, ts, approved, hash}. The hash is the run-mode
# same-issue hash (md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` over verdict-derive's
# --json output; legacy files hash their findings section).
fb_parse() {
  local f="$1" g="$2" rel vj tl pj hash
  rel="${f#"$root"/}"
  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then jq -nc --arg f "$rel" '{file: $f, exists: false}'; return 0; fi
  vj=$(bash "$VERDICT_DERIVE" --file "$f" --gate "$g" --json 2>/dev/null) || true
  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$vj" || vj='{"trailer_found":false,"verdict":null,"counts":null,"exit_code":1}'
  tl=$(grep -E '^<!-- LOA-VERDICT \{.*\} -->[[:space:]]*$' "$f" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1) || tl=""
  pj=$(printf '%s' "$tl" | sed -E 's/^<!-- LOA-VERDICT (.*) -->[[:space:]]*$/\1/')
  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$pj" || pj='{}'
  if [[ "$(jq -r '.trailer_found' <<<"$vj")" == true ]]; then
    hash=$(printf '%s\n' "$vj" | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
  else
    hash=$( { grep -A 100 "## Findings\|## Issues\|## Changes Required" "$f" 2>/dev/null || true; } | head -50 | _md5)
  fi
  jq -nc --arg f "$rel" --argjson v "$vj" --argjson p "$pj" --arg h "$hash" '
    def sid: if type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$") then . else null end;
    def tsv: if type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$") then . else null end;
    {file: $f, exists: true, trailer: ($v.trailer_found == true),
     verdict: ($v.verdict | if type == "string" then . else null end),
     counts: ($v.counts // null), exit_code: ($v.exit_code // 1),
     sprint_id: ($p.sprint_id | sid), ts: ($p.ts | tsv), hash: $h}
    | .approved = (.exit_code == 0 and .verdict == "APPROVED")'
}

# impl_commit SINCE → "sha epoch" of the newest non-merge commit on HEAD since
# SINCE touching a path outside the state/generated set, or nothing
impl_commit() {
  git -C "$root" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  git -C "$root" log --no-merges -n 1 --format='%H %ct' ${1:+"--since=$1"} -- . \
    ':(exclude,glob)grimoires/**' ':(exclude,glob).run/**' ':(exclude,glob)**/REPO-MAP.md' \
    ':(exclude,glob)**/checksums.json' ':(exclude,glob)**/CHANGELOG.md' 2>/dev/null || true
}

# The ordered rounds of one sprint directory: every -rN file, then the current
# file unless it is byte-identical to the highest -rN of its gate
rounds_of() {
  local dir="$1" g base f n top topn cur
  for g in review audit; do
    if [[ "$g" == review ]]; then base=engineer-feedback; else base=auditor-sprint-feedback; fi
    top=""; topn=-1
    for f in "$dir/$base"-r*.md; do
      [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
      n=${f##*-r}; n=${n%.md}
      [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]{1,6}$ ]] || continue
      fb_parse "$f" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" --argjson n "$((10#$n))" '. + {gate: $g, round: $n}'
      if (( 10#$n > topn )); then topn=$((10#$n)); top="$f"; fi
    done
    cur="$dir/$base.md"
    if [[ -f "$cur" ]] && ! { [[ -n "$top" ]] && cmp -s "$cur" "$top"; }; then
      fb_parse "$cur" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" '. + {gate: $g, round: 999999}'
    fi
  done
}

# Shared jq definitions: time, the breaker recompute and the run-state resolution
JQ_DEFS='
def epoch: if type == "string" then (sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) else null end;
def fresh($now; $win): epoch as $t | $t != null and ($now - $t) <= $win and ($t - $now) <= 300;
def recompute($rounds; $reset):
  ($rounds
   | map(select($reset == null or ((.ts // "") > $reset)))
   | sort_by([(.ts // ""), .round, (if .gate == "review" then 0 else 1 end)])
   | map(select(.approved | not))) as $nr
  | reduce $nr[] as $r ({cycle: 0, same: 0, hash: null, np: 0, lc: null};
      .cycle += 1
      | (if $r.hash != "none" and $r.hash == .hash then .same += 1 else .same = 1 | .hash = $r.hash end)
      | ($r.counts | tojson) as $c
      | (if .lc != null and .lc == $c then .np += 1 else .np = 0 end)
      | .lc = $c);
def skeleton($th; $ts):
  {state: "CLOSED",
   triggers: {same_issue: {count: 0, threshold: $th.same, last_hash: null},
              no_progress: {count: 0, threshold: $th.np},
              cycle_count: {current: 0, limit: $th.cycles},
              timeout: {started: $ts, limit_hours: $th.hours}},
   history: []};
def merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts):
  (if type == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
  | .triggers = (.triggers // {})
  | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ([(.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0), $rc.cycle] | max)
  | (if $rc.same > (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0)
     then .triggers.same_issue.count = $rc.same | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $rc.hash else . end)
  | (if $rc.np > (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) or (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts == null and $rc.lc != null)
     then .triggers.no_progress.count = ([(.triggers.no_progress.count // 0), $rc.np] | max)
          | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $rc.lc else . end)
  | ( if (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
        then ["same_issue", "same issue hash repeated \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times (derived from the feedback history)"]
      elif (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
        then ["no_progress", "counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds (derived from the feedback history)"]
      elif (.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
        then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds (derived from the feedback history)"]
      else null end ) as $trip
  | if $trip != null and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
    then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], source: "derive"}])
    else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end;
def known_ids: (.derivation.sprint_ids // null) // ((.sprints.list // []) | map(.id? // empty));
def resolve($f; $now; $win):
  . as $c
  | (if ($c | type) == "object" then $c else {} end) as $c
  | ($c.state // $c.status // "") as $cs
  | ($c | known_ids) as $known
  | ([$f.sprints[] | select(.state != "complete")
      | "sprint-\(.global_id)" as $g | .local_label as $l
      | select(($known | index($g)) == null and ($l == "" or ($known | index($l)) == null))] | length > 0) as $new
  | ((($c.completion // {}) | .merged_sha? // "") | type == "string" and length > 0) as $merged
  | if ($c.state // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or ($c.status // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or $merged then "JACKED_OUT"
    elif $f.breaker_open or $cs == "HALTED" then "HALTED"
    elif $f.all_complete then "COMPLETE"
    elif $cs == "COMPLETE" and ($new | not) then "COMPLETE"
    elif ($c.timestamps.last_activity? // null) | fresh($now; $win) then "RUNNING"
    else "INTERRUPTED" end;
'

cmd_derive() {
  local ledger="$root/grimoires/loa/ledger.json" a2a="$root/grimoires/loa/a2a" active rows
  if [[ ! -f "$ledger" ]] || ! jq -e 'type == "object"' "$ledger" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "run-checkpoint: derive: no readable ledger at $ledger — callers keep the cache" >&2; return 4
  fi
  active=$(jq -r '.active_cycle // empty | strings' "$ledger")
  if [[ -z "$active" ]] || ! jq -e --arg c "$active" 'any(.cycles[]?; .id == $c)' "$ledger" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "run-checkpoint: derive: the ledger has no active cycle — callers keep the cache" >&2; return 4
  fi
  local win now now_ts fa=1 th
  win=$(( $(cfg_int '.run_mode.stale_hours' 12 8760) * 3600 ))
  [[ "$(cfg '.run_mode.file_authoritative')" == false ]] && fa=0
  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
  now=$(date +%s); now_ts=$(now_iso)

  # Per-sprint facts
  local sprints="[]" gid label lstatus since dir rv au mex msid ic sj
  rows=$(jq -r --arg c "$active" '
    (.cycles[] | select(.id == $c)) as $cy
    | ($cy.sprints // [])[]
    | select((.global_id | type) == "number")
    | [(.global_id | tostring), ((.local_label // "") | tostring), ((.status // "") | tostring),
       ([.started, .created, $cy.created] | map(select(type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-")))
        | if length == 0 then "" else ([.[0], ($cy.created // "")] | max) end)]
    | map(if . == "" then "-" else . end)
    | @tsv' "$ledger")
  # "-" stands for an empty field: IFS whitespace (tab) would collapse two adjacent separators
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r gid label lstatus since; do
    [[ "$gid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
    [[ "$label" == - ]] && label=""
    [[ "$since" == - ]] && since=""
    [[ "$label" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$ ]] || label=""
    [[ "$lstatus" =~ ^[a-z_]{1,32}$ ]] || lstatus="unknown"
    [[ "$since" =~ ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$ ]] || since=""
    dir="$a2a/sprint-$gid"
    rv=$(fb_parse "$dir/engineer-feedback.md" review)
    au=$(fb_parse "$dir/auditor-sprint-feedback.md" audit)
    mex=false; msid=""
    if [[ -f "$dir/COMPLETED" ]]; then
      mex=true
      msid=$(sed -n 's/^sprint:[[:space:]]*\([A-Za-z0-9._-]*\).*/\1/p' "$dir/COMPLETED" | head -n 1) || msid=""
    fi
    ic=$(impl_commit "$since")
    sj=$(jq -nc --argjson gid "$gid" --arg label "$label" --arg status "$lstatus" --argjson rv "$rv" --argjson au "$au" \
              --argjson mex "$mex" --arg msid "$msid" --arg ic "$ic" '
      def mine: type == "string" and length > 0 and (. == "sprint-\($gid)" or ($label != "" and . == $label));
      ($rv.approved == true and ($rv.sprint_id | mine)) as $R
      | ($au.approved == true and ($au.sprint_id | mine)) as $A
      | ([$rv.sprint_id, $au.sprint_id, (if $msid == "" then null else $msid end)] | map(select(type == "string" and length > 0))) as $ids
      | ($mex and any($ids[]; mine | not)) as $stale
      | ($mex and ($stale | not) and (($rv.sprint_id | mine) or ($au.sprint_id | mine))) as $M
      | ($ic | split(" ")) as $c
      | ([$rv.ts, $au.ts] | map(select(. != null)) | max) as $vts
      | def verdict($x): if $x.exists then {verdict: $x.verdict, sprint_id: $x.sprint_id, consistent: ($x.exit_code == 0), file: $x.file} else null end;
      {global_id: $gid, local_label: $label, status: $status,
       completed_marker: $M, marker_present: $mex, stale_marker: $stale,
       review: verdict($rv), audit: verdict($au),
       impl_commit: (if ($c | length) == 2 then $c[0] else null end),
       commit_after_verdict: (if ($c | length) == 2 and $vts != null
                              then (($c[1] | tonumber) > ($vts | sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch 0)) else null end),
       legacy_feedback: ([$rv, $au] | map(select(.exists and (.trailer | not)) | .file)),
       state: (if $M and $R and $A and $status == "completed" then "complete"
               elif ($M | not) and $R and $A then "awaiting_marker" else "in_progress" end)}')
    sprints=$(jq -c --argjson s "$sj" '. + [$s]' <<<"$sprints")
  done <<<"$rows"

  # Breaker recompute over the active sprint's ordered rounds
  local active_gid rounds cache="null" cache_ok=1 bcache="null" reset rc merged
  active_gid=$(jq -r 'if length == 0 then "" else ((map(select(.state != "complete")) | .[0]) // .[-1]) | .global_id | tostring end' <<<"$sprints")
  rounds="[]"
  if [[ -n "$active_gid" && -d "$a2a/sprint-$active_gid" ]]; then
    rounds=$(rounds_of "$a2a/sprint-$active_gid" | jq -sc '.')
  fi
  if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
    if cache=$(jq -c . "$file" 2>/dev/null) && [[ -n "$cache" ]]; then :; else cache="null"; cache_ok=0; fi
  fi
  if [[ -f "$breaker" ]]; then bcache=$(jq -c 'if type == "object" then . else null end' "$breaker" 2>/dev/null) || bcache="null"; [[ -n "$bcache" ]] || bcache="null"; fi
  reset=$(jq -c '.reset_at? // null | if type == "string" then . else null end' <<<"$bcache")
  rc=$(jq -nc --argjson r "$rounds" --argjson z "$reset" "$JQ_DEFS"' recompute($r; $z)')
  merged=$(jq -c --argjson rc "$rc" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"' merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts)' <<<"$bcache")

  local facts report
  facts=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$sprints" --argjson b "$merged" '
    {sprints: $s,
     all_complete: (($s | length) > 0 and all($s[]; .state == "complete")),
     breaker_open: ($b.state == "OPEN"),
     stale_markers: [$s[] | select(.stale_marker) | "sprint-\(.global_id)"],
     legacy_feedback: [$s[] | .legacy_feedback[]],
     sprint_ids: [$s[] | "sprint-\(.global_id)"]}')
  report=$(jq -nc --argjson f "$facts" --argjson c "$cache" --argjson b "$merged" --argjson rc "$rc" \
                  --argjson now "$now" --argjson win "$win" --arg ts "$now_ts" --arg cycle "$active" \
                  --argjson fa "$fa" --argjson cache_ok "$cache_ok" --arg ag "$active_gid" "$JQ_DEFS"'
    def st: if type == "string" then (if test("^[A-Z_]{1,32}$") then . else "INVALID" end) else null end;
    ($c | resolve($f; $now; $win)) as $s
    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.state | st) else null end) as $cs
    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.status | st) else null end) as $cst
    | {cycle: $cycle, derived_at: $ts, stale_hours: ($win / 3600), file_authoritative: ($fa == 1),
       state: $s, cache_state: $cs, cache_status: $cst,
       cache: (if $cache_ok == 0 then "unparseable" elif $c == null then "missing" else "present" end),
       drift: ($c != null and ($cs != $s or ($cst != null and $cst != $s))),
       notes: ([
         (if $cs != null and $cst != null and $cs != $cst then "cache .state \($cs) and .status \($cst) disagree" else empty end),
         (if $s == "JACKED_OUT" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "JACKED_OUT is terminal: files show incomplete sprints; the cache is kept" else empty end),
         (if $s == "COMPLETE" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "COMPLETE kept: no new incomplete sprint in the ledger" else empty end),
         ($f.sprints[] | select(.stale_marker) | "sprint-\(.global_id): COMPLETED marker names another sprint (stale_marker, not counted)"),
         ($f.sprints[] | select(.state == "awaiting_marker") | "sprint-\(.global_id): review and audit APPROVED, no COMPLETED marker")
       ]),
       sprints: $f.sprints,
       active_sprint: (if $ag == "" then null else "sprint-\($ag)" end),
       breaker: {state: $b.state, cycle_count: $b.triggers.cycle_count.current, same_issue: $b.triggers.same_issue.count,
                 no_progress: $b.triggers.no_progress.count, recomputed: {cycle_count: $rc.cycle, same_issue: $rc.same, no_progress: $rc.np}},
       derivation: {source: "files", stale_markers: $f.stale_markers, legacy_feedback: $f.legacy_feedback},
       written: false}')

  if (( write )); then
    local why=""
    if (( fa == 0 )); then why="run_mode.file_authoritative: false — report-only"
    elif [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then why="no run state at $file — nothing to rewrite"
    elif (( cache_ok == 0 )); then why="$file unparseable — kept for inspection, not rewritten"
    fi
    if [[ -z "$why" ]]; then
      atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson rc "$rc" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"' merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts)' || return 3
      merged=$(jq -c . "$breaker")
      facts=$(jq -c --argjson b "$merged" '.breaker_open = ($b.state == "OPEN")' <<<"$facts")
      atomic_update "$file" --argjson f "$facts" --argjson now "$now" --argjson win "$win" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"'
        resolve($f; $now; $win) as $s
        | .state = $s | .status = $s | .derived_at = $ts
        | .derivation = {source: "files", stale_markers: $f.stale_markers, legacy_feedback: $f.legacy_feedback, sprint_ids: $f.sprint_ids}
        | .schema_version = (.schema_version // 2)' || return 3
      report=$(jq -c --slurpfile c "$file" --argjson b "$merged" '.written = true | .state = $c[0].state | .breaker.state = $b.state' <<<"$report")
    else
      report=$(jq -c --arg w "$why" '.notes += [$w]' <<<"$report")
    fi
  fi

  if (( json )); then
    jq . <<<"$report"
  else
    jq -r '"derive: files say \(.state), cache said \(.cache_state // "nothing") (\(if .drift then "drift" else "in sync" end))"
           + (if .written then " — caches rewritten" else "" end), (.notes[] | "  note: " + .)' <<<"$report"
  fi
  return 0
}

cmd_record_round() {
  [[ -n "$gate" && -n "$file" ]] || usage
  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: record-round: no feedback file at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
  local p th ts now out trip
  p=$(fb_parse "$file" "$gate")
  if [[ "$(jq -r '.approved' <<<"$p")" == true ]]; then
    echo "recorded: $gate APPROVED — breaker counters unchanged"
    return 0
  fi
  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
  ts=$(now_iso); now=$(date +%s)
  atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson p "$p" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$ts" --argjson now "$now" \
      --arg gate "$gate" --arg sprint "$sprint" "$JQ_DEFS"'
    (if type == "object" and (.triggers | type) == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
    | ($p.counts | tojson) as $c
    | (if $p.hash != "none" and $p.hash == (.triggers.same_issue.last_hash // null)
       then .triggers.same_issue.count = ((.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) + 1)
       else .triggers.same_issue.count = 1 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $p.hash end)
    | (if (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts // null) != null and .triggers.no_progress.last_counts == $c
       then .triggers.no_progress.count = ((.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) + 1)
       else .triggers.no_progress.count = 0 end)
    | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $c
    | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ((.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) + 1)
    | (.triggers.timeout.started // null | epoch) as $start
    | ( if .triggers.same_issue.count >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
          then ["same_issue", "same issue hash \($p.hash[0:8]) seen \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times in a row"]
        elif .triggers.no_progress.count >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
          then ["no_progress", "finding counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds"]
        elif .triggers.cycle_count.current >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
          then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds reached the limit \(.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)"]
        elif $start != null and ($now - $start) >= ((.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) * 3600)
          then ["timeout", "run older than \(.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) hours"]
        elif (.state // "CLOSED") == "OPEN" then ["open", "breaker already OPEN"]
        else null end ) as $trip
    | .last_round = {gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end), verdict: $p.verdict, hash: $p.hash, ts: $ts}
    | if $trip != null and $trip[0] != "open" and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
      then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end)}])
      elif $trip != null then .state = "OPEN"
      else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end
    | .last_trip = $trip' || return 3
  trip=$(jq -r '.last_trip // empty | if type == "array" then "\(.[0]): \(.[1])" else empty end' "$breaker")
  out=$(jq -r '"recorded: \(.last_round.gate) \(.last_round.verdict // "no verdict") — cycle \(.triggers.cycle_count.current)/\(.triggers.cycle_count.limit), same_issue \(.triggers.same_issue.count)/\(.triggers.same_issue.threshold), no_progress \(.triggers.no_progress.count)/\(.triggers.no_progress.threshold)"' "$breaker")
  echo "$out"
  if [[ -n "$trip" ]]; then
    atomic_update "$state_file" --arg ts "$ts" '.state = "HALTED"' || return 3
    echo "TRIPPED: $trip"
    return 10
  fi
  return 0
}

cmd_mark() {
  [[ -n "$skill" && -n "$sprint" ]] || usage
  mkdir -p "$run_dir"
  atomic_update "$run_dir/implement-active.json" --arg k "$skill" --arg s "$sprint" --arg ts "$(now_iso)" \
    '{skill: $k, sprint: $s, started_at: $ts}' || return 3
  if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
    local err drc=0
    err=$( { write=1; json=0; cmd_derive >/dev/null; } 2>&1 ) || drc=$?
    if (( drc != 0 && drc != 4 )); then printf '%s\n' "$err" >&2; fi
  fi
  echo "marked: $skill $sprint ($run_dir/implement-active.json)"
}

case "$sub" in
  write)  cmd_write ;;
  read)   cmd_read ;;
  derive) cmd_derive ;;
  record-round) cmd_record_round ;;
  mark)   cmd_mark ;;
  unmark) rm -f -- "$run_dir/implement-active.json" "$run_dir/implement-active.json.lock"; echo "unmarked" ;;
  *) usage ;;
esac

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# loa-kf-surface.sh — SessionStart hook (cycle-115 sprint-1, D1).
#
# Surfaces a compact symptom -> KF table from grimoires/loa/known-failures.md
# at session start so an agent sees the operational-failure log before
# triaging. DEFAULT-OFF: gated on `known_failures.surface_at_session_start`
# (default false) in .loa.config.yaml.
#
# STREAM ROUTING: Claude Code's SessionStart contract injects a hook's STDOUT
#   (on exit 0) into the session as context; STDERR is transcript-only and never
#   reaches the agent. This surface is only useful IN CONTEXT, so every ENABLED
#   path — the healthy table AND the enabled-but-degraded WARNINGs — writes to
#   STDOUT (an agent under the index-first intake contract must SEE that the KF
#   surface is degraded so it falls back to regenerating the index). Sibling
#   surfacing hooks (loa-l6-surface-handoffs.sh, loa-l7-surface-soul.sh) route
#   the same way. The DISABLED path emits nothing at all.
#
# CONTRACT (loud-but-nonblocking — this is OBSERVABILITY, never a gate):
#   - It MUST exit 0 in ALL paths. It MUST NOT block a session.
#   - When the flag is DISABLED (or config/yq absent): emit NOTHING, exit 0.
#   - When ENABLED but the surface is degraded — known-failures.md unreadable,
#     or zero KF entries parsed — emit a visible "[KF-SURFACE] WARNING ..."
#     to STDOUT and exit 0 (loud + in-context, so the agent notices a broken
#     knowledge surface; never silent on an enabled-but-broken path).
#   - When ENABLED and healthy: emit a compact symptom -> KF table to STDOUT,
#     exit 0.
#
# TRUST BOUNDARY: known-failures.md bodies are UNTRUSTED at surfacing. Every
#   field is control-byte-sanitized + length-capped before reaching session
#   context; body prose is NEVER interpreted as instructions (CLAUDE.md
#   agent-network universal invariant).
# =============================================================================
set -uo pipefail

HOOK_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${HOOK_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"

# --- test-mode seam (mirrors L4/L6/L7 cycle-098 gate): the config + path
#     overrides are honored ONLY under LOA_KF_SURFACE_TEST_MODE=1 with a bats
#     marker present. In production neither override is consulted. -----------
_kf_test_mode_active() {
  [[ "${LOA_KF_SURFACE_TEST_MODE:-0}" == "1" ]] || return 1
  [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}" ]] && return 0
  [[ -n "${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]] && return 0
  return 1
}

# Sanitize: drop control bytes (keep UTF-8 multibyte), flatten whitespace, cap.
_san() { printf '%s' "${1-}" | tr -d '\000-\010\013\014\016-\037\177' | tr '\t\n\r' '   ' | sed -E 's/  +/ /g; s/^ //; s/ $//' | cut -c1-100; }

# --- resolve enabled flag -----------------------------------------------------
enabled="false"
if _kf_test_mode_active && [[ -n "${LOA_KF_SURFACE_TEST_CONFIG-}" ]]; then
  # In test mode the override stands in for the parsed config value.
  enabled="${LOA_KF_SURFACE_TEST_CONFIG}"
else
  config_path="${REPO_ROOT}/.loa.config.yaml"
  # No yq or no config -> the feature is opt-in and unconfigurable here: silent.
  if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -f "$config_path" ]]; then
    # Explicit key, else the loa.profile default (cycle-129 D-9.1).
    # shellcheck source=scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh
    source "${REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh" 2>/dev/null &&
      enabled="$(loa_knob known_failures.surface_at_session_start false 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
  fi
fi

# DISABLED (or unconfigurable) -> emit nothing, exit 0. This is the ONLY silent path.
[[ "$enabled" == "true" ]] || exit 0

# --- ENABLED: from here every exit is loud-or-table, always exit 0 -----------
KF_FILE="${REPO_ROOT}/grimoires/loa/known-failures.md"
if _kf_test_mode_active && [[ -n "${LOA_KNOWN_FAILURES_FILE:-}" ]]; then
  KF_FILE="${LOA_KNOWN_FAILURES_FILE}"
fi

if [[ ! -r "$KF_FILE" ]]; then
  echo "[KF-SURFACE] WARNING: known-failures.md is unreadable at ${KF_FILE} — the known-failures surface is enabled but degraded. Triage without it; check the file path."
  exit 0
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# loa-l7-surface-soul.sh — SessionStart hook (cycle-098 Sprint 7B).
#
# At session start, read SOUL.md (project root, descriptive identity doc),
# validate against the L7 schema, and surface the body wrapped in
# sanitize_for_session_start("L7", body) into the session context. Always
# silent (exit 0 with no stdout) when:
#   - soul_identity_doc.enabled is not true in .loa.config.yaml
#   - SOUL.md is missing
#   - the config file is absent or malformed
#   - schema_mode=strict and validation fails (NFR-Sec3 prescriptive
#     rejection or required-section absence)
#
# For enabled, existing files that pass preflight, attempts a soul.surface
# audit event: surfaced | schema-warning | schema-refused. Audit failures
# are non-fatal. Missing files and disabled L7 do not emit audit events.
# The shared payload schema permits file-missing and disabled outcomes for
# other callers; that permissiveness does not promise emission by this hook.
#
# FR-L7-1 (load at session start), FR-L7-2 (warn|strict), FR-L7-4 (cap +
# reference path), FR-L7-5 (single-fire — re-source no-ops via LOA_L7_SURFACED
# env marker), FR-L7-6 (silent on disabled / missing / refused).
#
# Trust boundary: the SOUL.md body is OPERATOR-AUTHORED but UNTRUSTED at
# surfacing. soul_load wraps the body via sanitize_for_session_start("L7",
# body) before reaching session context — never interpret as instructions.
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

HOOK_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${HOOK_DIR}/../../.." && pwd)"
LIB="${REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/lib/soul-identity-lib.sh"
[[ -f "$LIB" ]] || exit 0

# Cache scoped to session — re-source no-ops (FR-L7-5).
[[ "${LOA_L7_SURFACED:-0}" == "1" ]] && exit 0

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Test-mode env-gated path overrides (LOA_SOUL_TEST_CONFIG +
# LOA_SOUL_TEST_PATH). Honored ONLY under bats / LOA_SOUL_TEST_MODE=1 with a
# bats-detected ancestor. Mirrors L4/L6 cycle-098 patterns.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
_l7_test_mode_active() {
    # cycle-098 sprint-7 cypherpunk CRIT-1 remediation: require BOTH a
    # robust bats marker AND opt-in `LOA_SOUL_TEST_MODE=1`. Mirrors the
    # lib-side gate at .claude/scripts/lib/soul-identity-lib.sh.
    [[ "${LOA_SOUL_TEST_MODE:-0}" == "1" ]] || return 1
    [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}" ]] && return 0
    [[ -n "${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]] && return 0
    return 1
}

config_path="${REPO_ROOT}/.loa.config.yaml"
if _l7_test_mode_active && [[ -n "${LOA_SOUL_TEST_CONFIG:-}" ]]; then
    config_path="$LOA_SOUL_TEST_CONFIG"
fi

# Gate on yq availability + config presence.
command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
[[ -f "$config_path" ]] || exit 0

# Read enable / mode / max-chars / path keys. Silent on malformed YAML
# (each yq returns the default).
# The enable key: explicit, else the loa.profile default (cycle-129 D-9.1).
enabled="false"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh
if source "${REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh" 2>/dev/null; then
    if [[ "$config_path" != "${REPO_ROOT}/.loa.config.yaml" ]]; then
        enabled="$(LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$config_path" loa_knob soul_identity_doc.enabled false 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
    else
        enabled="$(loa_knob soul_identity_doc.enabled false 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
    fi
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# loa-decisions-surface.sh: SessionStart hook that surfaces pending decision rows.
#
# Prints up to 10 `proposed` then `open` rows of grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml (id, status,
# summary only) so the operator sees what awaits /decisions confirm. DEFAULT-OFF: gated on
# `decisions.surface_at_session_start` (default false) in .loa.config.yaml.
#
# CONTRACT (observability, never a gate; same as loa-kf-surface.sh):
#   - Exits 0 on every path and never blocks a session.
#   - Disabled or no config: prints nothing (read with yq, or a plain-text fallback without it).
#   - Enabled but Mike Farah yq v4 or jq is missing, or the ledger is unreadable or has an
#     unknown schema_version: one "[DECISIONS] WARNING ..." line on stdout.
#   - Enabled and healthy: the block on stdout (SessionStart injects stdout as context);
#     nothing when no row is open or proposed and no marker is stale.
#   - A stale .run/unattended.json (another session, or older than
#     decisions.unattended_marker_ttl_hours, default 24) adds one notice line.
#
# TRUST BOUNDARY: row text is agent-authored and UNTRUSTED. Only id, status and summary are
#   read; each summary is control-stripped (C0, C1, U+2028/9), angle brackets are replaced so
#   no tag can close the fence, and it is capped at 100 characters. The whole block is then
#   wrapped by the L6 data fence, sanitize_for_session_start L6 <block> --max-chars 2000
#   (context-isolation-lib.sh). Without that sanitizer the block is not printed.
# =============================================================================
set -uo pipefail

HOOK_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${HOOK_DIR}/../../.." && pwd)"

# Test seam (mirrors loa-kf-surface.sh): overrides are honoured only under
# LOA_DEC_SURFACE_TEST_MODE=1 with a bats marker present.
_dec_test_mode_active() {
  [[ "${LOA_DEC_SURFACE_TEST_MODE:-0}" == "1" ]] || return 1
  [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}" || -n "${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]]
}

have_yq4=0
if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ "$(yq --version 2>&1 || true)" == *mikefarah*"version v4."* ]]; then have_yq4=1; fi

# The config is read first (yq, or a plain-text fallback without it), so an enabled surface on a host
# without its tools says so instead of looking disabled.
config_path="${REPO_ROOT}/.loa.config.yaml"
enabled="false"
if _dec_test_mode_active && [[ -n "${LOA_DEC_SURFACE_TEST_CONFIG-}" ]]; then
  enabled="${LOA_DEC_SURFACE_TEST_CONFIG}"
elif [[ -f "$config_path" ]]; then
  if [[ $have_yq4 -eq 1 ]]; then
    # Explicit key, else the loa.profile default (cycle-129 D-9.1).
    # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh
    source "${REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh" 2>/dev/null &&
      enabled="$(loa_knob decisions.surface_at_session_start false 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
  else
    # top-level `decisions:` block, then an indented `surface_at_session_start: true`
    enabled="$(awk '
      /^[^[:space:]#]/ { blk = ($0 ~ /^decisions:[[:space:]]*(#.*)?$/) }
      blk && /^[[:space:]]+surface_at_session_start:[[:space:]]*true[[:space:]]*(#.*)?$/ { print "true"; exit }
    ' "$config_path" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  fi
fi
[[ "$enabled" == "true" ]] || exit 0

missing=""
[[ $have_yq4 -eq 1 ]] || missing="Mike Farah yq v4"
command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing="${missing:+${missing} and }jq"
if [[ -n "$missing" ]]; then
  echo "[DECISIONS] WARNING: the decisions surface is enabled but ${missing} is missing; rows are not shown. Install it, or set decisions.surface_at_session_start: false."
  exit 0
fi

     6	# No profile can reach the floor. The floor source is .claude/data/floor.yaml
     7	# (read here, never duplicated); its sha256 pin is READ from
     8	# tests/unit/guard-origins.bats (FLOOR_SHA256) so the two suites cannot
     9	# disagree. Under `lean` every floor surface reads byte-identically to
    10	# `standard`: the floor config keys (the two gate skills' flatline_protocol.*
    11	# config, destructive_command_guard.*, implement_gate.*, hounfour.locality),
    12	# verdict-derive.sh on fixture feedback files, the adversarial gate's

    14	# the FR-1.2b / FR-SZ probes, and user-invoked-commands.txt.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# guardrails-orchestrator.sh - Coordinate all guardrail checks
# =============================================================================
# Version: 1.0.0
# Part of: Input Guardrails & Tool Risk Enforcement v1.20.0
#
# Usage:
#   guardrails-orchestrator.sh --skill implementing-tasks --input "Implement feature X"
#   guardrails-orchestrator.sh --skill deploying-infrastructure --input "Deploy to prod" --mode autonomous
#   guardrails-orchestrator.sh --skill implementing-tasks --file input.txt --allow-high
#
# Output: JSON with final action and all check results
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

# =============================================================================
# Configuration
# =============================================================================

readonly SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
readonly SCRIPT_NAME="$(basename "$0")"
readonly PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
readonly CONFIG_FILE="$PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"

# Source cross-platform time utilities
# shellcheck source=time-lib.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/time-lib.sh"

# Scripts
readonly PII_FILTER="$SCRIPT_DIR/pii-filter.sh"
readonly INJECTION_DETECT="$SCRIPT_DIR/injection-detect.sh"
readonly DANGER_LEVEL="$SCRIPT_DIR/danger-level-enforcer.sh"
readonly GUARDRAIL_LOGGER="$SCRIPT_DIR/guardrail-logger.sh"

# Defaults
DEFAULT_MODE="interactive"

# =============================================================================
# Functions
# =============================================================================

show_help() {
    cat <<EOF
Usage: $SCRIPT_NAME [OPTIONS]

Orchestrate all guardrail checks for a skill invocation.

Required Options:
  --skill NAME      Skill identifier
  --input TEXT      Input text to validate (or use --file)
  --file PATH       Read input from file

Optional:
  --mode MODE       Execution mode: interactive (default) or autonomous
  --allow-high      Allow high-risk skills in autonomous mode
  --session-id ID   Session ID for trajectory correlation
  --no-log          Skip trajectory logging
  --parallel NAME   Run specific check in parallel mode
  -h, --help        Show this help message

Guardrail Checks (in order):
  1. danger_level    - Check skill risk level against mode
  2. pii_filter      - Detect and redact sensitive data (blocking)
  3. injection       - Detect prompt injection patterns (blocking)

Output (JSON):
  {
    "action": "PROCEED|WARN|BLOCK",
    "skill": "skill-name",
    "mode": "interactive|autonomous",
    "checks": [...],
    "redacted_input": "sanitized text",
    "latency_ms": N
  }

Examples:
  $SCRIPT_NAME --skill implementing-tasks --input "Implement feature X"
  $SCRIPT_NAME --skill deploying-infrastructure --input "Deploy" --mode autonomous
  $SCRIPT_NAME --skill implementing-tasks --file task.txt --allow-high
EOF
}

# Read config value with default
get_config() {
    local key="$1"
    local default="$2"

    if [[ -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then
        local value
        value=$(yq -r "$key // \"$default\"" "$CONFIG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "$default")
        if [[ "$value" == "null" ]]; then
            echo "$default"
        else
            echo "$value"
        fi
    else
        echo "$default"
    fi
}

# Check if guardrails are enabled: the explicit key, else the loa.profile
# default (cycle-129 D-9.1; `standard` reads false). get_config's `// default`
# would read an explicit false as the default.
# shellcheck source=lib/profile-lib.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/profile-lib.sh"
is_enabled() {
    local enabled
    enabled=$(loa_knob guardrails.input.enabled false)
    [[ "$enabled" == "true" ]]
}

# Check if specific guardrail is enabled
is_check_enabled() {
    local check="$1"
    local enabled
    enabled=$(get_config ".guardrails.input.${check}.enabled" "true")
    [[ "$enabled" == "true" ]]
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================

# =============================================================================
# Version: 1.0.0
# Part of: Input Guardrails & Tool Risk Enforcement v1.20.0
#
# Usage:
#   danger-level-enforcer.sh --skill implementing-tasks --mode autonomous
#   danger-level-enforcer.sh --skill deploying-infrastructure --mode autonomous --allow-high
#   danger-level-enforcer.sh --skill autonomous-agent --mode interactive

set -euo pipefail

# =============================================================================
# Configuration
# =============================================================================

readonly SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
readonly SCRIPT_NAME="$(basename "$0")"

    ["discovering-requirements"]="safe"

)

# Functions

Usage: $SCRIPT_NAME [OPTIONS]
26:readonly CONFIG_FILE="$PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
     3	# =============================================================================
     4	# tests/unit/run-checkpoint-record-round.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 2 Task 2.5
     5	# (PRD FR-4(f) AC-4.6; SDD D-4.6). `run-checkpoint.sh record-round` replaces the
     6	# run-mode SKILL's breaker prose: the same-issue hash from the derived verdict,
     7	# no-progress, cycle count, timeout; a trip writes OPEN + HALTED and exits 10.
     8	# All files live in a temp dir.
     9	# =============================================================================
    10	
    11	setup() {
    12	  REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    13	  CK="$REPO/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh"
    14	  VD="$REPO/.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh"
    15	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rcr.XXXXXX")"
    16	  mkdir -p "$T/.run" "$T/a2a"
    17	  B="$T/.run/circuit-breaker.json"
    18	  S="$T/.run/state.json"
    19	  printf '{"run_id":"r","state":"RUNNING","phase":"REVIEW"}\n' > "$S"
    20	}
    21	teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
    22	
    23	# fb NAME GATE VERDICT [MEDIUM] — a feedback file verdict-derive accepts
    24	fb() {
    25	  local prose
    26	  if [[ "$3" == APPROVED ]]; then
    27	    if [[ "$2" == review ]]; then prose='All good'; else prose="APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO"; fi
    28	  else
    29	    prose=$'# Feedback\n\n## Findings\n\n- MEDIUM: fix it'
    30	  fi
    31	  printf '%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"%s","verdict":"%s","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":%s,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-1","ts":"2026-06-01T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' \
    32	    "$prose" "$2" "$3" "${4:-0}" > "$T/a2a/$1"
    33	}
    34	
    35	_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }
    36	
    37	breaker() {  # $1 jq tweak over a CLOSED breaker started now
    38	  jq -n '{state: "CLOSED",
    39	          triggers: {same_issue: {count: 0, threshold: 3, last_hash: null}, no_progress: {count: 0, threshold: 5},
    40	                     cycle_count: {current: 0, limit: 20}, timeout: {started: (now | floor | todate), limit_hours: 8}},
    41	          history: []}'"${1:+ | $1}" > "$B"
    42	}
    43	
    44	rr() { run --separate-stderr bash "$CK" record-round --root "$T" --breaker "$B" --state-file "$S" --sprint sprint-1 "$@"; }
    45	
    46	@test "RCR-1 a CHANGES_REQUIRED review increments cycle_count.current, sets same_issue {count 1, last_hash} to the SKILL's derived hash, exit 0" {
    47	  breaker
    48	  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
    49	  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
    50	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    51	  [[ "$output" == "recorded: review CHANGES_REQUIRED — cycle 1/20, same_issue 1/3, no_progress 0/5" ]]
    52	  local want
    53	  want=$(bash "$VD" --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md" --gate review --json 2>/dev/null | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
    54	  run jq -r '[.state, .triggers.cycle_count.current, .triggers.same_issue.count, .triggers.same_issue.last_hash, (.history | length)] | map(tostring) | join(" ")' "$B"
    55	  [ "$output" = "CLOSED 1 1 $want 0" ]
    56	  [ "$(jq -r .state "$S")" = RUNNING ]
    57	}
    58	
    59	@test "RCR-2 the same hash again counts up; a different finding set resets same_issue to 1 with the new last_hash" {
    60	  breaker
    61	  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
    62	  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
    63	  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
    64	  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.count "$B")" = 2 ]
    65	  local h1; h1=$(jq -r .triggers.same_issue.last_hash "$B")
    66	  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 2
    67	  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"

    72	}
    73

    75	  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.threshold = 99'

    79	  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
    80	  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
    81	  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.no_progress.count "$B")" = 2 ]
    82	  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 3
    83	  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
    84	  [ "$(jq -r .triggers.no_progress.count "$B")" = 0 ]
    85	}
    86

    88	  breaker

    96	  run jq -r '[.state, (.history | length), .history[0].trigger, .history[0].gate, .history[0].sprint] | map(tostring) | join(" ")' "$B"
    97	  [ "$output" = "OPEN 1 same_issue audit sprint-1" ]
    98	  [ "$(jq -r '.state + " " + .run_id' "$S")" = "HALTED r" ]
    99	  # a further round on an OPEN breaker still exits 10 and does not duplicate the history entry
   100	  rr --gate audit --file "$T/a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
   101	  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
   102	  [ "$(jq -r '.history | length' "$B")" = 1 ]
   103	}
   104	
   105	@test "RCR-5 the cycle limit, the no-progress threshold and the timeout trip in that documented order" {
   106	  fb engineer-feedback.md review CHANGES_REQUIRED 1
   107	  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.threshold = 99 | .triggers.cycle_count.current = 19'
   108	  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
   109	  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
   110	  [[ "$output" == *"TRIPPED: cycle_count: 20 changes-required rounds reached the limit 20" ]]
   111	  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.threshold = 99 | .triggers.no_progress.count = 4 | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = "{\"critical\":0,\"high\":0,\"medium\":1,\"low\":0}"'
   112	  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
   113	  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
   114	  [[ "$output" == *"TRIPPED: no_progress: "* ]]
   115	  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.threshold = 99 | .triggers.timeout.started = (now - 9 * 3600 | floor | todate)'
   116	  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
   117	  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
   118	  [[ "$output" == *"TRIPPED: timeout: run older than 8 hours" ]]
   119	  [ "$(jq -r .history[-1].trigger "$B")" = timeout ]
   120	}
   121	
   122	@test "RCR-6 APPROVED leaves every counter and the run state as they were (exit 0)" {
   123	  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.count = 2 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = "abc" | .triggers.cycle_count.current = 4 | .triggers.no_progress.count = 1'
   124	  cp "$B" "$T/before"
   125	  fb engineer-feedback.md review APPROVED

   127	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   128	  [[ "$output" == "recorded: review APPROVED — breaker counters unchanged" ]]
   129	  cmp "$T/before" "$B"
   130	  [ "$(jq -r .state "$S")" = RUNNING ]
   131	}
   132

   134	  printf 'Looks fine\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"audit","verdict":"APPROVED","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":0,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-1","ts":"2026-06-01T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' > "$T/a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
   135	  rr --gate audit --file "$T/a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"

   138	  [ "$output" = "CLOSED 1 20 3 5 8" ]
   139	  printf '# Review\n\n## Findings\n\n- a legacy finding\n' > "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
   140	  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"

content.content:
**Output** (Claude Code PreToolUse contract): allow is a silent exit 0 with empty stdout; ask and deny are exit 0 with `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask"|"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"…"}}`. A top-level `decision` field is never emitted.

**Modes** (`implement_gate.mode` in `.loa.config.yaml`; `/loa` prints the effective mode through `implement-gate.sh --effective-mode`, so the status line and the hook share one parser). The position is the derived `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` (`run-checkpoint.sh derive`); it is *known* when the cache parses and its `derived_at` is within `run_mode.stale_hours` (12 h).

| Mode | Unsanctioned App-Zone write | Audit row |
|------|-----------------------------|-----------|
| `ask` (default; also unset or an unknown value) | ask | `ask/ask` |
| `telemetry` | allow silently | `telemetry/outside_run` |
| `deny` | deny while the position is known; ask when it is unknown (missing, stale, never derived or unparseable) | `deny/deny`, `ask/unknown_position` |

`implement_gate.claims: authoritative` is the tighten-only modifier: a model-authored non-implementation claim in `tool_input.active_skill` asks (or is denied where `deny` would deny anyway); an implementation claim never allows by itself; an absent claim falls through. The deny reason ends with the two remedies (run the write inside `/implement` or `/bug`, or set `implement_gate.mode: ask`).

**Sanctions** (checked in the order run, marker, override; each allows with its own row): a derived RUNNING cache with a fresh `derived_at` (`allow/sanctioned_run`); a fresh `.run/implement-active.json` marker, written by `run-checkpoint.sh mark` at the start of `implementing-tasks` and `bug-triaging` and removed by `unmark` at their end (`allow/sanctioned_marker`; a stale marker logs `stale_marker` and does not sanction); `LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE=1` (`allow/override`, logged only when nothing else sanctioned). The legacy state files below keep sanctioning as before. This repository stays on `ask` until the cycle's last commit (DEC-0168).

**Path rule**: the path is `tool_input.file_path`, or `tool_input.notebook_path` for NotebookEdit. A relative path resolves from the payload's `cwd`. The root is `PROJECT_ROOT`, else `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, else the hook's own location (`<root>/.claude/hooks/compliance/`), never the process cwd, which follows Claude's `cd`. Both sides are canonicalised. The path counts as App Zone (`src/`, `lib/`, `app/`, at any depth under the root) when its physical form (symlinks followed) or its logical form (symlinks kept) matches, compared lowercased.

**Legacy heuristic** (still a sanction in every mode): an App Zone write is allowed when one state file shows an active run that is at most 24 h old. The former `implement_gate.mode: authoritative` value is read as `ask` plus `claims: authoritative`.

| State file | Allows when | Freshness field |
|------------|-------------|-----------------|
| `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` | `state == RUNNING` and a `plan_id` | `.timestamps.last_activity` (over 24 h asks) |
| `.run/simstim-state.json` | `phase == implementation` | `.timestamps.last_activity` (absent, unparsable or over 24 h asks) |
| `.run/state.json` | `state == RUNNING` | `.timestamps.last_activity`, else `.updated_at` (absent, unparsable or over 24 h asks) |

**Decision matrix**:

| Write | Decision |
|-------|----------|
| Payload unparsable, `jq` missing, or a path that cannot be canonicalised | `ask` (fail-ask) |
| A trust input: `.run/state.json`, `.run/sprint-plan-state.json`, `.run/simstim-state.json`, `.run/implement-active.json`, `.run/platform-features.json`, `.run/audit.jsonl`, `.loa.config.yaml` | `ask` in every mode + `compliance.state_write` row (`decision: trust_input`) |
| Any other non-App-Zone path, or a payload without a path | `allow` |
| App Zone, `claims: authoritative`, non-implementation claim | `ask` (deny under `deny` with a known position) + `compliance.mode.model_signal` row |
| App Zone, sanctioned (run, marker, override, or a fresh legacy state file) | `allow` + the sanction's row |
| App Zone, unsanctioned | per the mode table above |

**Audit events** (plain rows in `.run/audit.jsonl`, not the signed `audit_emit` chain; model-authored values cut to 256 bytes and written with `jq -a`): one row per decision carrying `hook: implement-gate`, `action` (`allow`, `ask`, `telemetry`, `deny`), `decision` and `mode`; `compliance.state_write` for trust inputs; `compliance.mode.model_signal` per authoritative claim; `replay: true` under `LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1`. The guard register (`guard-yield.sh`) counts the ask and telemetry rows as the gate's yield. Paths and claims shown on stderr have control and format characters stripped.

**Accepted gaps**: writes through the Bash tool are not seen (the C-PROC-001 fence gap). The sanctions trust `.run/` files a Bash command can write (bead bd-taee); a marker and a trailer forged together with the right sprint id pass `derive`. A direct `/implement` without `/run` leaves no run cache, so its writes rely on the marker. `deny` reads the sprint-plan cache only: a `/run sprint-N` run that leaves only `.run/state.json` is an unknown position under `deny` and asks.

**Tests**: `tests/unit/implement-gate.bats` (33 cases: the mode × claims × write class × sanction × cache-state matrix), `tests/unit/compliance-hook.bats`, `tests/unit/run-checkpoint-derive.bats`.

## block-destructive-bash.sh — Full Pattern Set & Posture (moved from CLAUDE.loa.md)

Blocks 12 destructive shapes: `rm -rf` (context-aware: blocks `/`, `~`, `$HOME`, `*`, `.`, `./.git`; allows `./build`, `./node_modules`, `/tmp/*`), `git push --force`/`-f`, `git reset --hard`, `git clean -f`, `git branch -D`/force-delete, `git stash drop`/`clear`, `git checkout -- <path>`, SQL `DROP {DATABASE,TABLE,SCHEMA}`, `TRUNCATE`, `DELETE FROM` no-WHERE (multi-statement loop), `kubectl delete namespace`, `kubectl delete --all`/`-A`. Audit-log trail to `.run/audit.jsonl` on every block with sanitized command + matched substring. Ported from Anthropic DCG public pattern set (cycle-111).

git:
    # auto_push: Controls whether to push commits to remote
    #   - true: Push and create PR automatically (default, current behavior)
    #   - false: Never auto-push, keep all changes local
    #   - prompt: Ask before pushing (HITL confirmation)
    # Can be overridden with --local (forces false) or --confirm-push (forces prompt)
    auto_push: true
    # Always create PRs as drafts - this is hardcoded and cannot be changed
    create_draft_pr: true
    # Git-aware sync_run_mode (Issue #474)
    # Branch to diff against when inferring sprint completion from git history.
    base_branch: "main"
    # Regex pattern (grep -E) for sprint commit messages. Default matches
    # conventional commit markers like "feat(sprint-1): implementation".
    # Override if your project uses a different commit convention.
    sprint_commit_pattern: '^feat\(sprint-'

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Implement gate (cycle-129 FR-4(a); hook: .claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PreToolUse check on Write/Edit/NotebookEdit into the App Zone (src/, lib/, app/)
# outside an implementation run. A write is SANCTIONED (allowed, one audit row each) by:
#   - a RUNNING run cache (.run/sprint-plan-state.json or .run/state.json, fresh
#     last_activity, and derived_at within run_mode.stale_hours when present);
#   - .run/implement-active.json {skill: implement|bug, sprint, started_at} younger than
#     two hours (`run-checkpoint.sh mark` at the start of /implement and /bug, `unmark`
#     at the end); a stale or malformed marker is logged and does not sanction;
#   - LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE=1 in the session environment (audited, one row per write).
# An unsanctioned App-Zone write is then handled by `mode`:
#   ask        (default) asks for confirmation, as before, and logs one row per ask
#   telemetry  logs one row to .run/audit.jsonl and allows silently
#   deny       refuses the write when the derived run position is known (the cache parses
#              and its derived_at is within run_mode.stale_hours); an unknown position
#              (missing, not derived, stale, unparseable) asks instead, never allows.
#              The hook is a fence only in this mode.
# Writes to the gate's own inputs (.run state files, .run/audit.jsonl, the marker,
# .loa.config.yaml) ask in every mode and under every sanction.
# `claims: authoritative` is a tighten-only modifier for any mode: a model-authored
# tool_input.active_skill naming a non-implementation skill asks (or, under deny, is
# denied), and never allows by itself. The legacy `mode: authoritative` means

    local event

    [ "$(echo "$event" | jq -r '.phase')" = "karpathy_check" ]
    [ "$(echo "$event" | jq -r '.principle')" = "surgical_changes" ]
    [ "$(echo "$event" | jq -r '.verdict')" = "warn" ]

    [ "$(jq -r --arg k '$schema' '.[$k]' "$SCHEMA")" = "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.type' "$SCHEMA")" = "object" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.additionalProperties' "$SCHEMA")" = "false" ]
}
