+        marker_stale) jq -nc '{skill: "bug", sprint: "sprint-bug-9", started_at: (now - 3 * 3600 | floor | todate)}' > "$ROOT/.run/implement-active.json" ;;
+    esac
+}
+
+# $1 path $2 claims $3 override (1 or empty) — stdout/stderr split, LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1
+gate_cell() {
+    if [[ "$2" == authoritative ]]; then
+        jq -nc --arg p "$1" '{tool_name: "Write", tool_input: {file_path: $p, content: "x", active_skill: "review-sprint"}}' > "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stdin.json"
+    else
+        jq -nc --arg p "$1" '{tool_name: "Write", tool_input: {file_path: $p, content: "x"}}' > "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stdin.json"
+    fi
+    run --separate-stderr env -u LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE ${3:+LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE=$3} LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 \
+        bash -c 'cd "$1" && PROJECT_ROOT="$1" RUN_DIR="$1/.run" bash "$2" < "$3"' _ "$ROOT" "$GATE" "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stdin.json"
+}
+
+# allow | ask | deny | invalid:<stdout>
+decision3() {
+    if [[ -z "$output" ]]; then echo allow; return; fi
+    local d
+    d=$(jq -r 'if (has("decision") | not) and .hookSpecificOutput.hookEventName == "PreToolUse"
+                  and (.hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecisionReason | type == "string" and length > 0)
+               then .hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision else "invalid" end' <<<"$output" 2>/dev/null) || d=invalid
+    case "$d" in ask|deny) echo "$d" ;; *) echo "invalid:$output" ;; esac
+}
+
+# The expected "<decision> <row>" for one cell; row = action/decision of the write's decision row
+expect_cell() {
+    local mode="$1" claims="$2" wclass="$3" sanction="$4" cache="$5" sanctioned=0 known=0
+    [[ "$mode" == unset ]] && mode=ask
+    if [[ "$wclass" == trust ]]; then echo "ask ask/trust_input"; return; fi
+    case "$sanction" in run_fresh|marker_fresh|override) sanctioned=1 ;; esac
+    case "$cache" in fresh|run_fresh) known=1 ;; esac
+    if [[ "$claims" == authoritative ]]; then
+        if [[ "$mode" == deny ]] && (( ! sanctioned && known )); then echo "deny deny/deny"; else echo "ask ask/ask"; fi
+        return
+    fi
+    if (( sanctioned )); then
+        case "$sanction" in run_fresh) echo "allow allow/sanctioned_run" ;; marker_fresh) echo "allow allow/sanctioned_marker" ;; *) echo "allow allow/override" ;; esac
+        return
+    fi
+    case "$mode" in
+        ask) echo "ask ask/ask" ;;
+        telemetry) echo "allow telemetry/outside_run" ;;
+        deny) if (( known )); then echo "deny deny/deny"; else echo "ask ask/unknown_position"; fi ;;
+    esac
+}
+
+# Runs every claims × write × sanction × cache cell for one mode and checks decision, row, row count, replay flag
+run_mode_matrix() {
+    local mode="$1" claims wclass sanction cache path got want row rows n_note n
+    command -v yq >/dev/null || skip "yq not installed"
+    for claims in plain authoritative; do
+        cfg_gate "$mode" "$claims"
+        for wclass in app trust; do
+            if [[ "$wclass" == app ]]; then path="$ROOT/src/x.ts"; else path="$ROOT/.run/state.json"; fi
+            for sanction in none run_fresh run_stale marker_fresh marker_stale override; do
+                for cache in fresh stale missing unparseable; do
+                    case "$sanction" in run_*) [[ "$cache" == fresh ]] || continue; cache="$sanction" ;; esac
+                    cache_state "$cache"; marker_state "$sanction"
+                    rm -f "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl"
+                    gate_cell "$path" "$claims" "$([[ "$sanction" == override ]] && echo 1)"
+                    local cell="mode=$mode claims=$claims write=$wclass sanction=$sanction cache=$cache"
+                    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$cell: exit $status" >&2; return 1; }
+                    want=$(expect_cell "$mode" "$claims" "$wclass" "$sanction" "$cache")
+                    got="$(decision3)"
+                    [ "$got" = "${want%% *}" ] || { echo "$cell: expected ${want%% *}, got $got" >&2; return 1; }
+                    # the write's decision row: the claim row (model_signal), the trust row (state_write) or the gate row
+                    row=$(jq -sr 'map(select(.action != "note" and (.hook == "implement-gate"))) | if length == 1 then "\(.[0].action)/\(.[0].decision)" else "count:\(length)" end' "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl" 2>/dev/null) || row="no-rows"
+                    [ "$row" = "${want#* }" ] || { echo "$cell: expected row ${want#* }, got $row" >&2; cat "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl" >&2; return 1; }
+                    # a stale marker logs stale_marker (and never sanctions) whenever the run path did not sanction first
+                    n_note=$(jq -s 'map(select(.decision == "stale_marker")) | length' "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl")
+                    if [[ "$wclass" == app && "$sanction" == marker_stale ]]; then
+                        [ "$n_note" = 1 ] || { echo "$cell: expected one stale_marker row, got $n_note" >&2; return 1; }
+                    else
+                        [ "$n_note" = 0 ] || { echo "$cell: unexpected stale_marker row" >&2; return 1; }
+                    fi
+                    # every row this gate wrote carries replay: true under LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 (DEC-0167)
+                    n=$(jq -s 'map(select(.replay != true)) | length' "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl")
+                    [ "$n" = 0 ] || { echo "$cell: $n rows without replay: true" >&2; return 1; }
+                    # telemetry prints nothing at all
+                    if [[ "${want#* }" == telemetry/outside_run ]]; then
+                        [[ -z "$output" && -z "$stderr" ]] || { echo "$cell: telemetry printed something" >&2; return 1; }
+                    fi
+                done
+            done
+        done
+    done
+}
+
+@test "IG-24 matrix, implement_gate unset: behaves exactly as ask in every cell" {
+    run_mode_matrix unset
+}
+
+@test "IG-25 matrix, mode ask: unsanctioned App-Zone writes ask with one ask row; sanctions allow with their own row; trust inputs ask" {
+    run_mode_matrix ask
+}
+
+@test "IG-26 matrix, mode telemetry: an unsanctioned App-Zone write logs one outside_run row and prints nothing; a non-implementation claim still asks" {
+    run_mode_matrix telemetry
+}
+
+@test "IG-27 matrix, mode deny: deny only for an unsanctioned App-Zone write with a fresh derived cache; an unknown position asks; trust inputs ask" {
+    run_mode_matrix deny
+}
+
+@test "IG-28 the telemetry row has exactly the documented keys and a control-stripped path of at most 256 bytes; without LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY no replay key" {
+    command -v yq >/dev/null || skip "yq not installed"
+    cfg_gate telemetry plain
+    jq -nc --arg p "$ROOT/src/a"$'\x1b'"[31mb.ts" '{tool_name: "Write", tool_input: {file_path: $p, content: "x"}}' > "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stdin.json"
+    run --separate-stderr env -u LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY -u LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE bash -c 'cd "$1" && PROJECT_ROOT="$1" RUN_DIR="$1/.run" bash "$2" < "$3"' _ "$ROOT" "$GATE" "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stdin.json"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [ -z "$output" ]
+    [ -z "$stderr" ]
+    run jq -c 'keys' "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl"
+    [ "$output" = '["action","decision","hook","mode","path","ts"]' ]
+    run jq -r '[.hook, .action, .decision, .mode, .path] | join(" ")' "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl"
+    [ "$output" = "implement-gate telemetry outside_run telemetry $ROOT/src/a[31mb.ts" ]
+    run -1 env LC_ALL=C grep -q $'[\x01-\x09\x0b-\x1f\x7f]' "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl"
+    local long
+    long=$(printf 'k%.0s' {1..400})
+    rm -f "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl"
+    jq -nc --arg p "$ROOT/src/$long.ts" '{tool_name: "Write", tool_input: {file_path: $p, content: "x"}}' > "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stdin.json"
+    run --separate-stderr env -u LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY bash -c 'cd "$1" && PROJECT_ROOT="$1" RUN_DIR="$1/.run" bash "$2" < "$3"' _ "$ROOT" "$GATE" "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/stdin.json"
+    run jq -j '.path' "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl"
+    [ "$(printf '%s' "$output" | LC_ALL=C wc -c)" -le 256 ]
+}
+
+@test "IG-29 the deny reply is a valid PreToolUse deny naming the derived position; the legacy mode: authoritative is ask + claims authoritative" {
+    command -v yq >/dev/null || skip "yq not installed"
+    cfg_gate deny plain
+    cache_state fresh
+    marker_state none
+    gate_cell "$ROOT/src/x.ts" plain ""
+    [ "$(decision3)" = deny ]
+    run jq -r '.hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecisionReason' <<<"$output"
+    [ "$output" = "App Zone write with no active implementation run (derived position: COMPLETE); run /implement or /bug, or set implement_gate.mode: ask" ]
+    # mode: authoritative keeps working: ask, and a review claim asks even with a fresh RUNNING cache
+    printf 'implement_gate:\n  mode: authoritative\n' > "$ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
+    run bash "$GATE" --effective-mode "$ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
+    [ "$output" = "ask (claims: authoritative)" ]
+    cache_state run_fresh
+    gate_cell "$ROOT/src/x.ts" authoritative ""
+    [ "$(decision3)" = ask ]
+    gate_cell "$ROOT/src/x.ts" plain ""
+    [ "$(decision3)" = allow ]
+}
+
+@test "IG-30 --effective-mode reads no stdin and prints the effective mode: unset/unknown → ask, the three modes, the claims modifier" {
+    command -v yq >/dev/null || skip "yq not installed"
+    run bash "$GATE" --effective-mode "$ROOT/no-such.yaml" < /dev/null
+    [ "$output" = ask ]
+    printf 'implement_gate:\n  mode: bogus\n' > "$ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
+    run bash "$GATE" --effective-mode "$ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
+    [ "$output" = ask ]
+    local m
+    for m in ask telemetry deny; do
+        cfg_gate "$m" plain
+        run bash "$GATE" --effective-mode "$ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
+        [ "$output" = "$m" ]
+    done
+    cfg_gate telemetry authoritative
+    run bash "$GATE" --effective-mode "$ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
+    [ "$output" = "telemetry (claims: authoritative)" ]
+    # default config path is PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml
+    run env PROJECT_ROOT="$ROOT" bash "$GATE" --effective-mode
+    [ "$output" = "telemetry (claims: authoritative)" ]
+}
+
+@test "IG-31 the implementing-skill marker is a trust input: a Write-tool write to it asks in every mode, even under a sanction" {
+    command -v yq >/dev/null || skip "yq not installed"
+    local m
+    for m in ask telemetry deny; do
+        cfg_gate "$m" plain
+        cache_state run_fresh
+        rm -f "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl"
+        gate_cell "$ROOT/.run/implement-active.json" plain 1
+        [ "$(decision3)" = ask ] || { echo "$m: expected ask" >&2; return 1; }
+        run jq -r '[.event, .action, .decision, .mode] | join(" ")' "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl"
+        [ "$output" = "compliance.state_write ask trust_input $m" ]
+    done
+}
+
+@test "IG-32 a marker for another skill, without a sprint, or dated in the future does not sanction and logs stale_marker" {
+    command -v yq >/dev/null || skip "yq not installed"
+    cfg_gate ask plain
+    cache_state missing
+    local body
+    for body in '{skill: "review", sprint: "sprint-1", started_at: (now | floor | todate)}' \
+                '{skill: "implement", started_at: (now | floor | todate)}' \
+                '{skill: "implement", sprint: "sprint-1", started_at: (now + 3600 | floor | todate)}' \
+                '{skill: "implement", sprint: "sprint-1", started_at: "yesterday"}'; do
+        jq -nc "$body" > "$ROOT/.run/implement-active.json"
+        rm -f "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl"
+        gate_cell "$ROOT/src/x.ts" plain ""
+        [ "$(decision3)" = ask ] || { echo "$body: expected ask" >&2; return 1; }
+        run jq -sr 'map(.decision) | join(",")' "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl"
+        [ "$output" = "stale_marker,ask" ] || { echo "$body: rows $output" >&2; return 1; }
+    done
+    printf 'not json' > "$ROOT/.run/implement-active.json"
+    gate_cell "$ROOT/src/x.ts" plain ""
+    [ "$(decision3)" = ask ]
+}
+
+@test "IG-33 a RUNNING state.json whose derived_at is older than run_mode.stale_hours does not sanction; run_mode.stale_hours narrows the window" {
+    command -v yq >/dev/null || skip "yq not installed"
+    printf 'implement_gate:\n  mode: ask\nrun_mode:\n  stale_hours: 2\n' > "$ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
+    marker_state none
+    cache_state missing
+    jq -nc '{state: "RUNNING", derived_at: (now - 3 * 3600 | floor | todate), timestamps: {last_activity: (now | floor | todate)}}' > "$ROOT/.run/state.json"
+    gate_cell "$ROOT/src/x.ts" plain ""
+    [ "$(decision3)" = ask ]
+    jq -nc '{state: "RUNNING", derived_at: (now - 3600 | floor | todate), timestamps: {last_activity: (now | floor | todate)}}' > "$ROOT/.run/state.json"
+    gate_cell "$ROOT/src/x.ts" plain ""
+    [ "$(decision3)" = allow ]
+    # a sprint-plan cache derived 3 h ago is stale under stale_hours: 2 → deny falls back to ask
+    rm -f "$ROOT/.run/state.json"
+    printf 'implement_gate:\n  mode: deny\nrun_mode:\n  stale_hours: 2\n' > "$ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
+    jq -nc '{plan_id: "p", state: "COMPLETE", derived_at: (now - 3 * 3600 | floor | todate), timestamps: {last_activity: (now | floor | todate)}}' > "$ROOT/.run/sprint-plan-state.json"
+    rm -f "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl"
+    gate_cell "$ROOT/src/x.ts" plain ""
+    [ "$(decision3)" = ask ]
+    run jq -r '.decision' "$ROOT/.run/audit.jsonl"
+    [ "$output" = unknown_position ]
 }

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/profile-lib.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.7 (AC-2.9; PRD
# AC-9.1, AC-9.3; SDD D-9.1, D-9.3)
#
# .claude/data/profiles.yaml + .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh: precedence
# (explicit key > profile > fallback), every profile defines every key,
# `standard` equals the oracle captured before any reader changed
# (tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json), unknown profile, the
# mtime-keyed cache, the overrides line, the /loa Profile line, the readers
# that route through loa_knob, and the grep lint for direct reads.
# =============================================================================

bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0

setup() {
    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    LIB="$R/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh"
    PROFILES="$R/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
    ORACLE="$R/tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json"
    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
    CFG="$T/config.yaml"
    export LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$CFG"
    export LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE="$T/run/effective-config.json"
    : > "$CFG"
}

knob() { bash "$LIB" knob "$@"; }

@test "PL-1 every profile defines every key, and the key set is the nine optional keys" {
    run diff <(yq -r '.profiles.lean | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort) <(jq -r '.keys | keys[]' "$ORACLE" | sort)
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    for p in standard full; do
        run diff <(yq -r ".profiles.$p | keys | .[]" "$PROFILES" | sort) <(yq -r '.profiles.lean | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort)
        [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    done
    [ "$(yq -r '.profiles | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort | paste -sd, -)" = "full,lean,standard" ]
    [ "$(yq -r '.schema_version' "$PROFILES")" = "1" ]
    ! yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | grep -qx 'interview.pacing'
}

@test "PL-2 every profile value is a boolean; lean is all false and full all true" {
    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles[][] | tag] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "!!bool" ]
    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles.lean[]] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "false" ]
    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles.full[]] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "true" ]
}

@test "PL-3 standard equals the oracle captured before any reader changed" {
    local k want got
    while IFS= read -r k; do
        want=$(jq -r --arg k "$k" '.keys[$k].standard' "$ORACLE")
        got=$(yq -r ".profiles.standard[\"$k\"]" "$PROFILES")
        [ "$want" = "$got" ] || { echo "standard $k = $got, oracle $want"; return 1; }
    done < <(jq -r '.keys | keys[]' "$ORACLE")
    # Outside the two guardrail keys (whose default this cycle changes) the
    # oracle's standard IS the value the readers returned for the shipped example.
    run jq -r '.keys | to_entries[] | select(.key | startswith("guardrails.") | not)
               | select(.value.standard != .value.example_today) | .key' "$ORACLE"
    [ -z "$output" ]
    run jq -r '.keys | to_entries[] | select(.key | startswith("guardrails.")) | "\(.value.example_today)/\(.value.standard)"' "$ORACLE"
    [ "$output" = "$(printf 'true/false\ntrue/false')" ]
}

@test "PL-4 standard equals the post-cycle example defaults (explicit example value, else the reader's fallback)" {
    local k ex st
    while IFS= read -r k; do
        ex=$(yq -r ".$k" "$R/.loa.config.yaml.example")
        st=$(yq -r ".profiles.standard[\"$k\"]" "$PROFILES")
        if [ "$ex" = "null" ]; then
            ex=$(jq -r --arg k "$k" '.keys[$k].empty_config_today' "$ORACLE")
        fi
        [ "$ex" = "$st" ] || { echo "example $k = $ex, standard $st"; return 1; }
    done < <(yq -r '.profiles.standard | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES")
    [ "$(yq -r '.loa.profile' "$R/.loa.config.yaml.example")" = "standard" ]
    # Under the example config the lib resolves standard and no override.
    LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$R/.loa.config.yaml.example" run bash "$LIB" overrides
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ -z "$output" ]
}

@test "PL-5 precedence: explicit key beats the profile, the profile beats the fallback" {
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\nknown_failures:\n  surface_at_session_start: true\nkarpathy_principles:\n  diff_lines_per_task: 250\n' > "$CFG"
    [ "$(knob known_failures.surface_at_session_start false)" = "true" ]     # explicit
    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start true)" = "false" ]          # lean, not the fallback
    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning true)" = "false" ]   # lean
    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task 100)" = "250" ]        # non-profile key, explicit
    [ "$(knob run_mode.stale_hours 7)" = "7" ]                               # non-profile key, fallback
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: full\n' > "$CFG"
    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start false)" = "true" ]
    : > "$CFG"
    [ "$(bash "$LIB" profile)" = "standard" ]
    [ "$(bash "$LIB" source)" = "default" ]
    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning false)" = "true" ]   # standard, not the fallback
}

@test "PL-6 an explicit false is honoured (yq's // would read it as absent)" {
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: full\nguardrails:\n  input:\n    enabled: false\n  danger_level:\n    enforce: false\n' > "$CFG"
    [ "$(knob guardrails.input.enabled true)" = "false" ]
    [ "$(knob guardrails.danger_level.enforce true)" = "false" ]
    [ "$(knob .guardrails.input.enabled true)" = "false" ]                   # leading dot accepted
}

@test "PL-7 an unknown profile warns once on stderr and resolves standard" {
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: turbo\n' > "$CFG"
    run --separate-stderr bash "$LIB" profile
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ "$output" = "standard" ]
    [[ "$stderr" == *'unknown loa.profile "turbo"; using standard'* ]]
    [ "$(bash "$LIB" source 2>/dev/null)" = "invalid" ]
    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria false 2>/dev/null)" = "true" ]
    # A non-string profile is unknown too.
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: [lean]\n' > "$CFG"
    [ "$(bash "$LIB" profile 2>/dev/null)" = "standard" ]
}

@test "PL-8 the cache is written once and rebuilt when the config or profiles.yaml changes" {
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\n' > "$CFG"
    touch -d '2026-01-01 00:00:00' "$CFG"
    knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x >/dev/null
    [ -f "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.profile' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE")" = "lean" ]
    # Same stamps → served from the cache: a planted value proves the read path.
    jq '.knobs["decisions.surface_at_session_start"].value = "from-cache"' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE" > "$T/c" && mv "$T/c" "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x)" = "from-cache" ]
    # A config edit with a new mtime rebuilds.
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: full\n' > "$CFG"
    touch -d '2026-01-02 00:00:00' "$CFG"
    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x)" = "true" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.profile' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE")" = "full" ]
    # A profiles.yaml edit rebuilds too.
    cp "$PROFILES" "$T/profiles.yaml"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# run-checkpoint.sh — run position in .run/ (cycle-125 FR-3, SDD D-3.2;
# cycle-129 FR-4(f)/FR-5, SDD D-4.6, D-5.1 … D-5.4). Beads are the task ledger;
# the checkpoint is a HINT; the run state and the breaker are caches DERIVED
# from files (COMPLETED markers, LOA-VERDICT trailers, the ledger, git).
#
#   run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint sprint-N --phase PHASE [--task BEAD-ID] [--file F]
#       Atomically sets .schema_version = 2, .checkpoint = {sprint, task, phase, ts}
#       and .timestamps.last_activity = ts: jq → F.tmp.$$ → mv -f, under flock
#       on F.lock. F must already exist (a run in progress). Then runs
#       `derive --write` (a missing ledger is skipped). Exit 0 · 2 usage /
#       no run · 3 write failed (the previous file is untouched).
#   run-checkpoint.sh read [--file F] [--json]
#       Prints the checkpoint when it is trustworthy: parses, and when a task
#       is named, `br show <task> --json` reports it closed (a checkpoint that
#       names an open or unknown bead is DISCARDED with a logged line — beads
#       remain the recovery source). schema_version 1 / no checkpoint → prints
#       "sprint granularity". Exit 0 always when F exists; 2 when it does not.
#   run-checkpoint.sh derive [--json] [--write] [--root DIR] [--file F]
#       For the ledger's active cycle, per sprint: global_id, local_label,
#       ledger status, completed_marker (a2a/sprint-<gid>/COMPLETED exists and
#       the feedback trailers name this sprint, as sprint-<gid> or the local
#       label; a trailer or a `sprint:` line naming another sprint makes it a
#       stale_marker, treated as absent), review/audit verdicts (verdict-derive.sh;
#       APPROVED needs exit 0; a file without a trailer is legacy: no verdict,
#       listed in derivation.legacy_feedback), impl_commit (newest non-merge
#       commit on HEAD since max(sprint started|created, cycle created) touching
#       a path outside grimoires/, .run/, REPO-MAP.md, checksums.json,
#       CHANGELOG.md) and state complete | awaiting_marker | in_progress.
  esac
done

# Root and run dir: --root wins (and pins the run dir under it); else the
# directory holding a --file that sits in a .run/ dir (write/read/derive only);
# else this script's checkout with $LOA_RUN_DIR honoured.
if [[ -n "$root" ]]; then
  run_dir="$root/.run"
else
  root="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  run_dir="${LOA_RUN_DIR:-$root/.run}"
  if [[ -n "$file" && "$sub" != record-round ]]; then
    fdir="$(cd "$(dirname "$file")" 2>/dev/null && pwd)" || fdir=""
    if [[ -n "$fdir" && "$(basename "$fdir")" == .run ]]; then root="$(dirname "$fdir")"; run_dir="$fdir"; fi
  fi
fi
if [[ "$sub" != record-round && -z "$file" ]]; then file="$run_dir/sprint-plan-state.json"; fi
[[ -n "$breaker" ]] || breaker="$run_dir/circuit-breaker.json"
[[ -n "$state_file" ]] || state_file="$run_dir/state.json"
CONFIG="$root/.loa.config.yaml"

now_iso() { date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ; }

# cfg KEY → the raw yq value ("null" when absent or unreadable). yq's `//`
# treats false as absent, so callers compare the raw text.
cfg() {
  local v
  if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -f "$CONFIG" ]]; then
    v=$(yq "$1" "$CONFIG" 2>/dev/null) || v="null"
    printf '%s' "${v//\"/}"
  else
    printf 'null'
  fi
}
cfg_int() {  # KEY DEFAULT MAX → a positive integer ≤ MAX, else DEFAULT
  local v; v=$(cfg "$1")
  if [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( v > 0 && v <= $3 )); then printf '%s' "$v"; else printf '%s' "$2"; fi
}

_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }

# atomic_update FILE JQ-ARGS... — jq over FILE (or {} when FILE is absent) →
# FILE.tmp.$$ → mv -f, under flock on FILE.lock. Exit 3 on any failure; the
# previous file is untouched.
atomic_update() {
  local f="$1"; shift
  local tmp="$f.tmp.$$" rc=0
  (
    # flock is util-linux (Linux); without it (macOS) the write is still atomic
    # (tmp + mv) but concurrent writers may interleave — last writer wins.
    if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then flock -w 5 9 || { echo "run-checkpoint: lock timeout on $f.lock" >&2; exit 3; }; fi
    if [[ -f "$f" ]]; then
      jq "$@" "$f" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: $f is not valid JSON — not written" >&2; exit 3; }
    else
      jq "$@" <<<'{}' > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: could not build $f" >&2; exit 3; }
    fi
    jq -e . "$tmp" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: refusing to replace $f with unparseable output" >&2; exit 3; }
    mv -f -- "$tmp" "$f"
  ) 9>"$f.lock" || rc=$?
  return $rc
}

cmd_write() {
  [[ -n "$sprint" && -n "$phase" ]] || usage
  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: no run state at $file (start a run first)" >&2; return 2; fi
  local ts rc=0
  ts=$(now_iso)
  atomic_update "$file" --arg s "$sprint" --arg t "$task" --arg p "$phase" --arg ts "$ts" \
    '.schema_version = 2
     | .checkpoint = {sprint: $s, task: (if $t == "" then null else $t end), phase: $p, ts: $ts}
     | .timestamps = ((.timestamps // {}) + {last_activity: $ts})' || rc=$?
  (( rc == 0 )) || return $rc
  # Every checkpoint refreshes the derived caches (D-5.2); a missing ledger (4) is not an error here
  local err drc=0
  err=$( { write=1; json=0; cmd_derive >/dev/null; } 2>&1 ) || drc=$?
  if (( drc != 0 && drc != 4 )); then printf '%s\n' "$err" >&2; fi
  return 0
}

bead_closed() {  # $1 bead id → 0 when br reports closed
  command -v br >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 2
  local js st
  js=$(br show "$1" --json 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  st=$(printf '%s' "$js" | jq -r 'if type=="array" then .[0] else . end | .status // .issue.status // empty' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  [[ "$st" == "closed" ]]
}

cmd_read() {
  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: no run state at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
  if ! jq -e . "$file" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "run-checkpoint: $file unparseable — no checkpoint; beads are the recovery truth" >&2; if (( json )); then echo '{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"unparseable"}'; fi; return 0; fi
  local sv cp s t p ts reason="" brc
  sv=$(jq -r '.schema_version // 1' "$file"); cp=$(jq -c '.checkpoint // null' "$file")
  [[ "$sv" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || sv=1
  if [[ "$cp" == "null" || "$sv" -lt 2 ]]; then
    if (( json )); then echo '{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"sprint granularity"}'; else echo "checkpoint: none (schema_version $sv → sprint granularity; resume at the first open bead of sprints.current)"; fi
    return 0
  fi
  s=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.sprint // empty' "$file"); t=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.task // empty' "$file"); p=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.phase // empty' "$file"); ts=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.ts // empty' "$file")
  if [[ -z "$s" || -z "$p" ]]; then reason="malformed checkpoint"
  elif [[ -n "$t" ]]; then
    # A task checkpoint is trusted only when beads CONFIRMS the task closed;
    # "br unavailable" is not a confirmation (Bridgebuilder PR #1269 FIND-003).
    brc=0; bead_closed "$t" || brc=$?
    case $brc in 0) ;; 2) reason="beads unavailable — task $t cannot be verified";; *) reason="task $t is not closed in beads";; esac
  fi
  if [[ -n "$reason" ]]; then
    echo "run-checkpoint: discarding checkpoint ($reason) — resume from the first open bead of $s" >&2
    if (( json )); then jq -cn --arg r "$reason" --arg s "$s" '{checkpoint:null, reason:$r, sprint:$s}'; else echo "checkpoint: discarded ($reason); resume at the first open bead of $s"; fi
    return 0
  fi
  if (( json )); then jq -c '{checkpoint: .checkpoint}' "$file"
  else echo "checkpoint: $s ${t:+task $t }phase $p at $ts → resume at the first open bead after $t in $s"; fi
}

# fb_parse FILE GATE → one compact JSON object: {file, exists, trailer, verdict,
# counts, exit_code, sprint_id, ts, approved, hash}. The hash is the run-mode

I stopped this review partway through. A safety check halted my work while I was writing test commands that try to sneak dangerous commands past the hook, so I didn't continue that kind of testing. Most of the "fails open" checks you asked for were not run, and I can't claim the classifier is sound.

**What I confirmed by running it** (copies in `/tmp/rev-c`):
- The corpus runner on the head hook gives: benign 89/89, dangerous 142/142, residual 0/5 (runtime about 35.5s, p95 59ms).
- With a body containing a destructive command under an unquoted delimiter (`cat <<EOF`), the classifier returns `nonexec`, but the command stays visible in the scrub copy. So the per-segment scan keeps it and the hook still blocks (rc=2), the same as the base hook.

**Finding from reading the code (not reproduced):**

- `head/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/run-corpus.sh:101-102` — The runner always exits 0 in text and `--json` modes, even when there are mismatches. It prints them and the summary line, but nothing sets a failing exit status. `--rows` also exits 0 at line 87. Any CI step or caller that relies on the exit code will pass with mismatching rows unless it parses the output. I didn't check whether a bats test parses it. Confidence: medium.

**Checked and not a defect:** in `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh`, the jq/yq in-place check (`-[A-Za-z]*i*`) looks wrong next to its comment, but as a glob it only matches short-flag clusters that contain an `i`. So `jq -r` is not wrongly flagged.

**Not reviewed:**
- Nothing on the "fails open" list was tested against crafted inputs: `<<-` with tabs, quoted and backslash delimiters, several heredocs, here-strings, unterminated bodies, the same-line exec check on target names, the write-target checks, and the knob parser.
- I didn't review `danger-level-enforcer.sh`, `guardrails-orchestrator.sh` or `guard-yield.bats`, and I didn't audit the corpus's expected values row by row.

If you want, I can review those parts by reading the code alone, without running crafted dangerous inputs.

# =============================================================================
# Karpathy Principles (#961 enforcement v1)
# =============================================================================
# Mechanical reinforcement of the 4 Karpathy principles documented inline in
# .claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md (post-PR #960) and detailed in
# .claude/protocols/karpathy-principles.md.
#
# v1 ships:
#   - Surgical-Changes diff-size hook (warn-by-default, opt-in BLOCK reserved for v2)
#   - Goal-Driven success-criteria gate in /implement
#   - Trajectory logging at grimoires/loa/a2a/trajectory/karpathy-*.jsonl
karpathy_principles:
  # Advisory — used by skills' Think-Before-Coding internal checks. No hook
  # consumer in v1; reserved for v2 when surface-assumption analysis lands.
  surface_assumptions: true

  # Simplicity enforcement intensity: full (default, enforced — the YAGNI ladder,
  # stdlib/native first, shortest diff) or ultra (deletion-first, challenges the
  # requirement before building). There is NO advise-only 'lite' level: the
  # "never simplify away" floor (C-PROC-011) stays enforced at every level.
  simplicity_intensity: full

  # G-1 — master switch for the PostToolUse:Write|Edit surgical-diff hook
  # at .claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh. When false,
  # the hook fast-paths to exit 0 in <10ms.
  surgical_diff_warning: true

  # G-1 — per-session diff-lines threshold. When the session accumulator
  # exceeds this, the hook emits a [karpathy-surgical-warn] stderr line
  # and writes a trajectory event. Raised from the original protocol-doc
  # sketch of 50 because 50 was empirically too tight for bug-fix sprints
  # that legitimately touch 60-80 lines (test file + production diff).
  diff_lines_per_task: 100

  # Reserved for v2 — no v1 consumer. Cyclomatic complexity check.
  simplicity_check: true

  # Reserved for v2 — no v1 consumer. AST-level abstraction-depth analysis.
  max_abstraction_depth: 2

  # G-3 — when true, /implement refuses to write code if sprint.md lacks a
  # "Success criteria" / "Acceptance criteria" / "Verification" section.
  # Operator can [Skip with rationale] to override per-invocation.
  require_success_criteria: true

local hash_status
  hash_status=$(bash "$lint_dir/marker-utils.sh" verify-hash "$file" 2>/dev/null || echo "NO_HASH")
  case "$hash_status" in
    VALID) report "PASS" "claude-md" "CLAUDE.loa.md header integrity hash verifies (VALID)" ;;
    *)     report "WARN" "claude-md" "CLAUDE.loa.md header integrity hash check: ${hash_status} — re-stamp via .claude/scripts/marker-utils.sh update-hash" ;;
  esac

  # bug-989 review DISS-001: verify_hash compares the hex PREFIX only, so a
  # header glued by the pre-fix update_hash ("<correct-hex>PLACEHOLDER") still
  # verifies VALID. Flag the residue independently so installed-base repos get
  # the re-stamp signal too.
  if head -1 "$file" | grep -q 'PLACEHOLDER'; then
    report "WARN" "claude-md" "CLAUDE.loa.md header carries a PLACEHOLDER residue — re-stamp via .claude/scripts/marker-utils.sh update-hash"
  fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Invariant 3: constraints.json is valid JSON
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
check_constraints() {
  local file=".claude/data/constraints.json"

  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then
    report "WARN" "constraints" "constraints.json not found at $file"
    return
  fi

  if jq empty "$file" 2>/dev/null; then
    report "PASS" "constraints" "constraints.json is valid JSON"
  else
    report "ERROR" "constraints" "constraints.json is invalid JSON"
    if [[ "$AUTO_FIX" == "true" ]]; then
      echo "  Cannot auto-fix invalid JSON — manual repair needed"
    fi
  fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Invariant 4: Constraint-generated blocks exist in CLAUDE.loa.md
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
check_constraint_blocks() {
  local file=".claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"

  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then
    report "ERROR" "constraint-blocks" "CLAUDE.loa.md not found"
    return
  fi

  local block_count
  block_count=$(grep -c '@constraint-generated: start' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -z "$block_count" ]] && block_count=0

  if [[ "$block_count" -ge 3 ]]; then
    report "PASS" "constraint-blocks" "$block_count constraint-generated blocks found"
  elif [[ "$block_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
    report "WARN" "constraint-blocks" "Only $block_count constraint-generated blocks (expected 3+)"
  else
    report "ERROR" "constraint-blocks" "No constraint-generated blocks found"
  fi

  # Check start/end pairs match
  local start_count end_count
  start_count=$(grep -c '@constraint-generated: start' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  end_count=$(grep -c '@constraint-generated: end' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -z "$start_count" ]] && start_count=0
  [[ -z "$end_count" ]] && end_count=0

  if [[ "$start_count" -ne "$end_count" ]]; then
    report "ERROR" "constraint-blocks" "Mismatched start/end pairs: $start_count starts, $end_count ends"
  fi
}

+# Prints the heading of an optional table section; returns 1 when the section
+# is not optional.
+optional_table_heading() {
+  local section="$1" entry o_name o_heading
+  for entry in "${OPTIONAL_TABLES[@]}"; do
+    IFS='|' read -r o_name o_heading <<< "$entry"
+    if [[ "$o_name" == "$section" ]]; then
+      printf '%s\n' "$o_heading"
+      return 0
+    fi
+  done
+  return 1
+}
+
+# Removes an optional table block from FILE: the exact heading line, the
+# table-header lines between it and the start marker, the marker block, and
+# one blank line after the end marker. A file without the start marker is
+# already pruned (no-op). Anything else between the heading and the start
+# marker, a missing heading or a missing end marker is an error and leaves
+# FILE untouched.
+prune_optional_table() {
+  local file="$1" section="$2" heading="$3"
+  if ! grep -q "@constraint-generated: start ${section} " "$file"; then
+    verbose "Optional section ${section} already absent from ${file}"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  local tmp="${file}.prune-tmp" rc=0
+  awk -v heading="$heading" \
+      -v start="@constraint-generated: start ${section} " \
+      -v end="@constraint-generated: end ${section} " '
+    function flush(   i) { for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) print buf[i]; n = 0 }
+    state == "" && $0 == heading { state = "head"; n = 0; buf[++n] = $0; next }
+    state == "head" {
+      if (index($0, start)) { state = "skip"; n = 0; next }
+      if ($0 ~ /^\|/ || $0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*$/) { buf[++n] = $0; next }
+      flush(); state = ""; print; next
+    }
+    state == "skip" { if (index($0, end)) state = "after"; next }
+    state == "after" { state = "done"; if ($0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*$/) next }
+    { print }
+    END {
+      if (state == "head") flush()
+      if (state == "skip") exit 3
+      if (state == "" ) exit 4
+    }
+  ' "$file" > "$tmp" || rc=$?
+  if [[ "$rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
+    rm -f "$tmp"
+    case "$rc" in
+      3) log "ERROR: ${file}: no end marker for optional section '${section}'" ;;
+      4) log "ERROR: ${file}: optional section '${section}' has markers but no '${heading}' heading directly above its table" ;;
+      *) log "ERROR: ${file}: pruning optional section '${section}' failed (awk exit ${rc})" ;;
+    esac
+    return 1
+  fi
+  mv "$tmp" "$file"
+  verbose "Pruned empty optional section ${section} (${heading}) from ${file}"

# ============================================================================
# Bootstrap: insert markers into target files
# ============================================================================

# Anchor patterns: section_name|start_regex|end_regex
readonly -a ANCHORS=(
  "process_compliance_never|^### NEVER Rules$|^### |^---$"
  "process_compliance_always|^### ALWAYS Rules$|^### |^---$"
  "task_tracking_hierarchy|^### Task Tracking Hierarchy$|^$|^---$"
  "pre_implementation_checklist|^## Pre-Implementation Checklist$|^## |^---$"
  "autonomous_agent_constraints|AUTONOMOUS_SKILL_ANCHOR|AUTONOMOUS_SKILL_END"
  "simstim_constraints|SIMSTIM_SKILL_ANCHOR|SIMSTIM_SKILL_END"
  "implementing_tasks_constraints|IMPLEMENTING_SKILL_ANCHOR|IMPLEMENTING_SKILL_END"
)

bootstrap_section() {
  local file="$1"
  local section="$2"
  local content="$3"

  local hash
  hash=$(compute_section_hash "$content")

  local start_marker="<!-- @constraint-generated: start ${section} | hash:${hash} -->"
  local end_marker="<!-- @constraint-generated: end ${section} -->"
  local warning="<!-- DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/constraints.json -->"

  if grep -q "@constraint-generated: start ${section}" "$file"; then
    verbose "Section ${section} already has markers in ${file}, skipping bootstrap"
    return 0
  fi

  # Find anchor for this section
  local anchor_start="" anchor_end=""
  for anchor in "${ANCHORS[@]}"; do
    local a_section a_start a_end
    IFS='|' read -r a_section a_start a_end <<< "$anchor"
    if [[ "$a_section" == "$section" ]]; then
      anchor_start="$a_start"
      anchor_end="$a_end"
      break
    fi
  done

  if [[ -z "$anchor_start" ]]; then
    log "WARNING: No anchor defined for section ${section}, skipping"
    return 0
  fi

  # For skill-md sections, use <constraints> tags
  if [[ "$anchor_start" == *"SKILL_ANCHOR"* ]]; then
    verbose "Skill section ${section}: markers will be inserted inside <constraints> block during generation"
    return 0
  fi

  # Find the anchor line and insert markers after the table header
  local matches
  matches=$(grep -c "$anchor_start" "$file" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
  if [[ "$matches" -ne 1 ]]; then
    log "ERROR: Anchor '${anchor_start}' matches ${matches} times in ${file} (expected 1)"
    return 1
  fi

  # Find the section: locate header, keep table header+separator, wrap data rows with markers
  local tmp="${file}.bootstrap-tmp"
  local end_pat1="${anchor_end%%|*}"
  local end_pat2="${anchor_end#*|}"
  awk -v anchor="$anchor_start" \
      -v end_pat1="$end_pat1" \
      -v end_pat2="$end_pat2" \
      -v start_m="$start_marker" \
      -v warning_m="$warning" \
      -v end_m="$end_marker" \
      -v content_m="$content" \
      '
      BEGIN { state="looking"; sep_seen=0 }
      state == "looking" && $0 ~ anchor {
        print; state="in_header"; next
      }
      state == "in_header" {
        # Print everything until we see the separator row (|---|)
        print
        if ($0 ~ /^\|[-|: ]+\|$/) {
          sep_seen=1
          print start_m
          print warning_m
          printf "%s\n", content_m
          state="skipping"
        }
        next
      }
      state == "skipping" {
        if ($0 ~ end_pat1 || $0 ~ end_pat2) {
          print end_m
          if ($0 !~ /^$/) print
          state="done"
          next
        }
        # Skip original data rows (replaced by generated content)
        next
      }
      state != "skipping" { print }
      END {
        if (state == "skipping") print end_m
      }
      ' "$file" > "$tmp"

  if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]] && [[ "$BOOTSTRAP_CONFIRM" != "true" ]]; then
    diff -u "$file" "$tmp" || true
    rm -f "$tmp"
  else
    mv "$tmp" "$file"
    log "Bootstrapped markers for section '${section}' in ${file}"
  fi
}

# ============================================================================
# Main generation pipeline
# ============================================================================

generate_all_sections() {
  # Phase 0: Build target -> sections map
  declare -A target_sections
  declare -A section_data  # section -> "target|template|filter"

  for entry in "${SECTIONS[@]}"; do
    local s_name s_target s_template s_filter
    IFS='|' read -r s_name s_target s_template s_filter <<< "$entry"

    if [[ -n "$SECTION_FILTER" ]] && [[ "$s_name" != "$SECTION_FILTER" ]]; then
      continue
    fi

    if [[ ! -f "$s_target" ]]; then
      log "WARNING: Target file not found: $s_target, skipping"
      continue
    fi

    target_sections["$s_target"]+="${s_name} "
    section_data["$s_name"]="${s_target}|${s_template}|${s_filter}"
  done

  if [[ ${#target_sections[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
    log "No sections to generate"
    return 0
  fi

  # Phase 1: Create staged copies
  declare -A staged_files
  trap 'for tmp in "${staged_files[@]}"; do rm -f "$tmp"; done' EXIT

  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    local tmp
    tmp=$(mktemp "${target}.constraint-XXXXXX")
    cp "$target" "$tmp"
    staged_files["$target"]="$tmp"
  done

  # Phase 2: Render and apply all sections to staged copies
  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    local tmp="${staged_files[$target]}"
    for section in ${target_sections[$target]}; do
      local s_data="${section_data[$section]}"
      local s_target s_template s_filter
      IFS='|' read -r s_target s_template s_filter <<< "$s_data"

      local o_heading
      if o_heading=$(optional_table_heading "$section"); then
        local o_rows
        o_rows=$(jq -r "$s_filter | length" "$REGISTRY")
        if [[ "$o_rows" == "0" ]]; then
          if [[ "$BOOTSTRAP" != "true" ]] && ! prune_optional_table "$tmp" "$section" "$o_heading"; then
            log "ERROR: Generation failed for section '${section}' — no files modified"
            return 1
          fi
          continue
        fi
      fi

      verbose "Rendering section: $section"
      local content
      content=$(render_section "$section" "$s_template" "$s_filter")

      if [[ "$BOOTSTRAP" == "true" ]]; then
        bootstrap_section "$tmp" "$section" "$content"
      else
        if ! insert_generated_section "$tmp" "$section" "$content"; then
          log "ERROR: Generation failed for section '${section}' — no files modified"
          return 1
        fi
      fi
    done
  done

  # Phase 3: Diff or commit
  if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]] && [[ "$BOOTSTRAP_CONFIRM" != "true" ]]; then
    for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
      log "Diff for ${target}:"
      diff -u "$target" "${staged_files[$target]}" || true
    done
    for tmp in "${staged_files[@]}"; do rm -f "$tmp"; done
    trap - EXIT
    return 0
  fi

  # Commit with rollback
  declare -A backup_files
  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    local bak="${target}.constraint-bak"
    cp "$target" "$bak"
    backup_files["$target"]="$bak"
  done

  local commit_failed=false
  local committed=()
  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    if mv "${staged_files[$target]}" "$target"; then
      committed+=("$target")
    else
      commit_failed=true
      break
    fi
  done

  if [[ "$commit_failed" == "true" ]]; then
    local rollback_ok=true
    for t in "${committed[@]}"; do
      if ! cp -f "${backup_files[$t]}" "$t"; then
        rollback_ok=false
      fi
    done
    for tmp in "${staged_files[@]}"; do rm -f "$tmp"; done
    if [[ "$rollback_ok" == "true" ]]; then
      for bak in "${backup_files[@]}"; do rm -f "$bak"; done
      log "ERROR: Commit failed — all targets rolled back"
    else
      log "ERROR: Commit failed — rollback partially failed, .constraint-bak files preserved"
    fi
    trap - EXIT
    return 1
  fi

  # Success: clean up backups and update @loa-managed hashes
  for bak in "${backup_files[@]}"; do rm -f "$bak"; done
  trap - EXIT

  # Phase 4: Update @loa-managed hashes (IMP-002)
  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    if bash "$MARKER_UTILS" has-marker "$target" | grep -q "true"; then
      verbose "Updating @loa-managed hash for ${target}"
      bash "$MARKER_UTILS" update-hash "$target"
    fi
  done

  log "Generation complete: ${#target_sections[@]} target(s) updated"
}

I found two real defects, two low-severity gaps and one minor prose inconsistency. Everything else in scope checks out.

I ran these in `/tmp/rev-d` (yq v4.40.5, jq and bats are installed). `profile-lib.bats` passed 15 of 17. PL-14 and PL-15 failed only because the PR snapshot is missing the repo files they call (loa-status, bash-version-guard, pii-filter and others); I don't count those as defects. `floor.yaml` isn't in the snapshot either, so I tested against a stub floor file. `check-knob-readers.sh` passes on the snapshot tree.

## Findings

1. **`head/.claude/data/profiles.yaml:42`** — `standard` sets `invisible_retrospective.enabled: true`, which quietly changes the old default.
   - Before this PR, the reader was the rendered prose in `base/.claude/data/skill-includes/retrospective_postlude.md:1` (also in implementing-tasks, reviewing-code and auditing-security SKILL.md). It ran the scan only on an explicit `invisible_retrospective.enabled: true`, so a missing key meant off.
   - This repo's `.loa.config.yaml` doesn't set the key. Running `profile-lib.sh json` on the head tree shows `"invisible_retrospective.enabled": {"value": true, "source": "profile"}`. So the retrospective scan now runs after every implement, review and audit here, and in any install whose config lacks the key.
   - The PR's own oracle records the old values (`head/tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json:60-61`: `this_repo_today: false`, `empty_config_today: false`).
   - The header comment at `profiles.yaml:14-15` says only the two guardrail keys change default, which is wrong here. PL-4 hides it because it compares against the example's explicit `true`, not the reader's fallback. The fix is either `standard: false`, or documenting this as a migration item the way the guardrail keys are.
   - Confidence: high.

2. **`head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:78`** — the cache key loses its file timestamps when one of the three input files is missing.
   - On Linux, if any of config / profiles.yaml / floor.yaml is absent, the first `stat -Lc` prints lines for the files that exist but exits 1. That triggers the BSD fallback `stat -Lf '%N|%Fm|%z'`.

- **Guardrail keys:** `guardrails.input.enabled` and `guardrails.danger_level.enforce` do flip from true to false for configs without the keys, including the enforcer with no config file. `.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh write` (atomic, locked); `task` is the last CLOSED bead
(`null` for a phase-only checkpoint). Readers accept 1 and 2; a missing or discarded checkpoint
means sprint granularity (resume at the first open bead of `sprints.current`).

rewrites `.state` (canonical) and `.status` (its mirror) from the files and adds
`"derived_at": "<ISO-8601>"` and
`"derivation": {"source": "files", "stale_markers": [], "legacy_feedback": [], "sprint_ids": []}`;
`schema_version` is kept. Files without these keys are read as before. The decision table is
in the script header; `run_mode.file_authoritative: false` makes it report-only.

+
+These five rules govern every team. The ids stay as names.

+| Id | Rule | Why |
+|----|------|-----|
+| C-TEAM-001 | Planning, orchestration, deployment and lifecycle skills are lead-only; teammates implement, review and audit only (the Skill Invocation Matrix below is the full list) | Planning skills produce single artifacts (PRD, SDD, sprint plan) that assume single-writer semantics; concurrent invocation would corrupt state |

content.content:
All subsequent `.run/*.json` mutations in this skill MUST use the atomic write pattern: pipe the
`jq` transform to a `.tmp` sibling, then `mv` the `.tmp` file over the original — never edit the
JSON file in place.

## Main Loop — Single Sprint (`/run sprint-N`)

```
while circuit_breaker.state == CLOSED:
  1. /implement $target
  2. Commit changes, then track deletions (see "Deleted Files Tracking" below)
  3. update_state(phase: REVIEW); checkpoint(phase: REVIEW)
  4. /review-sprint $target
  5. If `verdict-derive.sh --gate review` on engineer-feedback.md does not exit 0 with
     `.verdict == APPROVED` (anything else — including an inconsistent trailer — counts as
     findings) → record-round (see "Circuit Breaker" below); exit 10, HALT; else continue
     loop (back to step 1)
  6. update_state(phase: AUDIT); checkpoint(phase: AUDIT)
  7. /audit-sprint $target
  8. If `verdict-derive.sh --gate audit` on auditor-sprint-feedback.md does not exit 0 with
     `.verdict == APPROVED` → same as step 5 (golden-path's `_gp_sprint_is_audited` additionally
     re-derives the review trailer and cross-checks `excluded` ⇔ `excluded_confirmed`)
  9. RED_TEAM_CODE gate (if enabled) — see resources/conditional-procedures.md §red-team-code-gate
  10. If COMPLETED marker exists → update_state(state: COMPLETE); break
Create draft PR (see "Completion and PR Creation" — resources/completion-modes.md)
Invoke Post-PR Validation if enabled — resources/conditional-procedures.md §post-pr-validation
Update state to READY_FOR_HITL or JACKED_OUT
```

Call `check_rate_limit` (see "Rate Limiting" below) before each of steps 1, 4, and 7.
`checkpoint(...)` = `.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint $target --phase <PHASE>`
(when `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` exists); `/implement` writes the per-task checkpoint on each
`br close`. Beads stay the recovery truth — the checkpoint is a hint `/run-resume` reports.

## Circuit Breaker

After each `/review-sprint` and `/audit-sprint`, run
`.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh record-round --gate review|audit --file <feedback-file> --sprint $target`.
It updates `.run/circuit-breaker.json` (same-issue hash, no-progress, cycle count, timeout; thresholds in that
file and `run_mode.defaults`); exit 10 has already written `OPEN` and `HALTED` — report its
`TRIPPED: <trigger>: <reason>` line, then "Run halted. Use `/run-resume --reset-ice` to continue."

### Red Team Code-vs-Design Circuit Breaker

Separate counter from the main circuit breaker (see `resources/conditional-procedures.md`
§red-team-code-gate for behavior).

content.text:
I found six real problems that this change introduces, plus three small ones. The two worth fixing first are 1 and 2: each one denies writes during a legitimate implementation run. I reproduced findings 1, 2, 3 and 6 by running copies in `/tmp/rev-b`; 4 and 5 rest on reading the code. The PR's new bats cases IG-24 to IG-33 all pass here (bats, jq 1.6, mikefarah yq 4.40.5), so none of these is covered by the tests.

**1. `head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:550` — the marker expires after two hours and nothing renews it, so `/implement` gets denied partway through its own run.** Confidence: medium-high.
- `check_implement_marker` only accepts `started_at` within 7200 s.
- `head/.claude/skills/implementing-tasks/SKILL.md:229` (and `bug-triaging`) say to `mark` once at the start and `unmark` at the end, with no refresh step.
- `mark` also runs `derive --write`, which sets `derived_at` to now on any existing sprint-plan cache. That turns an "unknown" position into a "known" one for `run_mode.stale_hours` (12 h).
- So under `deny`, a direct `/implement` or `/bug` that runs past two hours is denied for up to the next ten hours. The deny text then tells the user to "run /implement or /bug", which they are already doing.
- Reproduced: leftover COMPLETE cache with a fresh `derived_at`, marker aged 2 h 1 m, App-Zone write gives `deny` with rows `note/stale_marker` and `deny/deny`.

**2. `head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:505` (window fixed at line 470) — deny fires while the derived position is RUNNING.** Confidence: medium.
- The run sanction requires `last_activity` within a hard-coded 24 h (`_ig_fresh`).
- `derive` marks a run RUNNING when `last_activity` is within `run_mode.stale_hours`, and that setting can go up to 8760.
- With `stale_hours: 48` and `last_activity` 30 h old, the cache is RUNNING with a fresh `derived_at`, yet the gate denies with "no active implementation run (derived position: RUNNING)" (reproduced).
- The same contradiction happens when a RUNNING cache has no `plan_id` (line 498 returns early).
- The deny branch at line 629 never checks whether `position_state` is RUNNING. Lines 566–567 also deny a known cache that has no `state`, labelled "unknown", while the docs say an unknown position asks.

**3. `head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:485-486` — a `derived_at` that is not a string skips the freshness check (fails open).** Confidence: medium on the logic, low on practical impact.
- `.derived_at // empty | strings` treats `0`, `false` or an epoch number as "no `derived_at`", and that returns success.
- Reproduced: `state.json {state: RUNNING, derived_at: 0, fresh last_activity}` gives `allow/sanctioned_run` under `deny`. A stale string date correctly asks.
- `read_position` treats the same value as "not derived", so the two checks disagree. Reaching this needs a Bash write to a trust input, which the docs list as an accepted gap.

**4. `head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:510-511` — the new `derived_at` check returns from the whole function on failure.** Confidence: low-medium.
- When it fails, the `simstim-state.json` and `state.json` sanctions are never checked.
- A leftover sprint-plan cache (last activity under 24 h, `derived_at` over 12 h) therefore removes the sanction for an active `/simstim` implementation phase or a `/run` with a fresh `state.json`. The result is an ask in every mode.
- The old code fell through to those files when the sprint-plan state was not RUNNING.

**5. `head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:196` — `stale_hours` is read differently from `run-checkpoint.sh`.** Confidence: low.
- The gate keeps only numbers (`.s | numbers`), so a quoted `stale_hours: "24"` is ignored and it uses 12.
- `run-checkpoint.sh` `cfg_int` strips quotes and uses 24.
- The two components then disagree on the window. This only makes the gate stricter (more asks), but it is the same knob read two ways.

**6. `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378` (used at lines 380 and 389) — `derive` cannot run on jq 1.6.** Confidence: high (verified). Outside my main scope, but it changes how the gate behaves.
- `--arg label` binds `$label`, and `label` is a reserved word in jq 1.6: `jq -n --arg label x '$label'` gives a syntax error, exit 3.
- On jq 1.6 every `derive --write` (including the one inside `mark`) fails with "is not valid JSON — not written", so `derived_at` is never written.
- Effect on the gate: `deny` never denies (always `ask/unknown_position`), and the derived-cache sanction never applies. Renaming the variable (e.g. `$lbl`) fixes it.

**Smaller items (low confidence):**
- **`head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:548` vs `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:88`** — `mark --sprint` accepts any length, but the gate only accepts 1–64 characters. A longer sprint id is marked successfully yet never sanctions, and logs `stale_marker`.
- **`head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:175` and line 340** — `mark` writes the marker under `LOA_RUN_DIR`, while the gate reads `RUN_DIR` (default `<root>/.run`). Separately, the trust-input patterns hard-code `.run/`, so with a non-default `RUN_DIR` the real marker and state files have no Write/Edit protection.
- **`head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:590-593`** — a stale marker plus the override writes two rows (`note/stale_marker` and `allow/override`), while `.loa.config.yaml.example` and the header say one row per write.

Everything else I checked held up and matches the docs: path normalisation for trust inputs (`../`, `./`, case, logical vs physical), trust-input asks in every mode and under every sanction, the deny output shape, unknown position falling back to ask, `--effective-mode`, the `guard-origins.yaml` note matching the `hooks-reference.md` row, and the "33 cases" test count.

- The old code fell through to those files when the sprint-plan state was not RUNNING.

**5. `head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:196` — `stale_hours` is read differently from `run-checkpoint.sh`.** Confidence: low.
- The gate keeps only numbers (`.s | numbers`), so a quoted `stale_hours: "24"` is ignored and it uses 12.
- `run-checkpoint.sh` `cfg_int` strips quotes and uses 24.
- The two components then disagree on the window. This only makes the gate stricter (more asks), but it is the same knob read two ways.

**6. `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378` (used at lines 380 and 389) — `derive` cannot run on jq 1.6.** Confidence: high (verified). Outside my main scope, but it changes how the gate behaves.
- `--arg label` binds `$label`, and `label` is a reserved word in jq 1.6: `jq -n --arg label x '$label'` gives a syntax error, exit 3.

Separately, the trust-input patterns hard-code `.run/`, so with a non-default `RUN_DIR` the real marker and state files have no Write/Edit protection.

## git-aware-state-sync

### Git-Aware State Sync (cycle-056, Issue #474)

When context compaction or session loss leaves `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` stuck at
`state: "RUNNING"` with `0` completed sprints — even though git history shows all sprint commits
already landed — `simstim-orchestrator.sh --sync-run-mode` cross-references git as a secondary
source of truth before returning `still_running`.

**When the fallback fires** (all three must hold):
1. `sprint-plan-state.json` shows `state: "RUNNING"` (the normal trigger)
2. `sprints.total` (or `sprints.list` length) resolves to a positive integer
3. `git log ${base_branch}..HEAD` shows at least `sprints.total` commits matching
   `run_mode.git.sprint_commit_pattern`

When satisfied: updates `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` to `state: "JACKED_OUT"` with
`git_inferred: true` and an ISO-8601 `git_inferred_at` timestamp; returns
`{ "synced": true, "reason": "git_inferred_completion", "commits_found": N, "commits_expected": M, "base_branch": "main" }`.

**When it does NOT fire**: in-flight runs with no commits yet, or partial runs
(`commits_found < commits_expected`) → existing `still_running` preserved; state already
`JACKED_OUT`/`HALTED` → existing validation flow.

     8	#   block    → dangerous: the hook must exit 2

+# =============================================================================
+# FR-6 heredoc consumer classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1; knob
+# destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier, default true; false = the
+# pre-cycle scan, i.e. only the #1245 quoted-cat scrub below).
+# Defined BEFORE the bash-version guard and the stdin read so another script
+# can source this file with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 and call
+#   _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   → prints interpreter|nonexec|none
+#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>               → exit 0 iff nonexec
+# Bash 3.2 compatible (no ${x,,}, no mapfile, no associative arrays) and safe
+# under a caller's `set -u`.
+#
+# Grammar (literal command text; no alias or function expansion; CRLF folded
+# to LF). The command is walked line by line; a line holding an unquoted
+# `<<` / `<<-` (not `<<<`) is a heredoc header, the body runs to the first
+# line equal to the delimiter (leading tabs stripped for `<<-`). FULL SCAN
+# (the whole command as today) on: any other control character, a header the
+# tokenizer cannot read (open quote, trailing backslash, comment), more than
+# one heredoc on a header, a delimiter that is not a plain word ('W', "W",
+# \W or W with W in [A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]; `$X` is a variable delimiter), or a
+# missing terminator. Per heredoc the class is:
+#   interpreter — body scanned exactly as today: the header holds `$(`, a
+#     backtick, `<(` or `>(`, a paren or brace group or a shell keyword; it
+#     continues on the next line (`|`, `&&`, `||` last) or an earlier line
+#     opened a substitution, group, quote or pipe; a member of the heredoc's
+#     pipeline is a shell, interpreter, wrapper that runs its argument or SQL
+#     runner (_bdb_hd_is_interp, _bdb_hd_is_runner); an allowlisted form
+#     carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag (-c, -e, -x clusters, --exec,
+#     --eval, --command, in-place); a write target is executable content
+#     (_bdb_hd_exec_dest: script extension, .claude/hooks, .claude/settings*
+#     .json, .git/hooks, .git/config, rc/profile files, /etc, a bin dir or a
+#     directory on PATH, or any non-literal path); the first body line is a
+#     shebang; the body holds `<<` (nested); a target's basename appears
+#     elsewhere in the command outside the safe readers (_bdb_hd_same_line_exec:
+#     `bash x`, `./x`, `source x`, `. x`, `chmod +x x`, `exec x`, cp/mv …).
+#   nonexec — every pipeline member is an exact allowlisted form
+#     (_bdb_hd_member): cat, tee, printf, echo with plain-file or stdout sinks;
+#     gh pr|issue comment -F -; gh pr create --body-file -; git commit -F -;
+#     br create|update reading `-`; jq/yq without in-place; grep; sed -n with
+#     a print-only script; sort; wc. The body is then scanned PER SEGMENT
+#     (_bdb_hd_scan_body): each line split on ; && || | &, wrapper prefixes
+#     stripped (sudo command exec env nice time nohup builtin stdbuf ionice,
+#     a leading backslash, quote, paren or brace, assignments, an absolute
+#     path); a segment whose command word is a fence verb (rm git find dd
+#     mkfs* shred truncate kubectl terraform aws gcloud psql mysql DROP
+#     DELETE TRUNCATE) is kept on its own line for the normal rules, other
+#     segments are dropped. The body falls back to a full scan when it holds
+#     `$(`, a backtick, `<(` or `>(` under an unquoted delimiter, or a segment
+#     word is an interpreter or wrapper, or a variable (`$x -rf /`; such a

+#     Special case (the #1245 scrub): a standalone quoted-delimiter `cat`

+_bdb_hd_op_re='^[0-9]*(<<<|<<-|&>>|<<|>>|>[|]|&&|[|][|]|[|]&|&>|<>|>&[0-9-]*|<&[0-9-]*|;;|;|&|[|]|<|>|[(]|[)])$'

+_bdb_hd_re_ddq='^"([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)"$'
+_bdb_hd_re_dbs='^\\([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)$'

+# Shells, interpreters and wrappers that run their argument or stdin.
+_bdb_hd_is_interp() {

+    bash|sh|zsh|dash|ksh|mksh|ash|fish|csh|tcsh|busybox|python|python[0-9]*|pypy*|node|nodejs|deno|bun|ruby|irb|perl|php|lua|luajit|tclsh|wish|expect|pwsh|powershell|osascript|Rscript) return 0 ;;
+    eval|source|.|exec|command|builtin|time|awk|gawk|mawk|nawk|make|gmake|m4|ed|ex|vi|vim|nvim|gdb) return 0 ;;

+  return 1

+# The SQL runners of the FR-1.4/5/6 precondition (same list).
+_bdb_hd_is_runner() {

+  return 1

+_bdb_hd_is_destructive() {

+    rm|git|find|dd|shred|truncate|kubectl|terraform|aws|gcloud|psql|mysql|mkfs|mkfs.*) return 0 ;;

+  return 1

+_bdb_hd_is_safe_reader() {

+    cat|ls|wc|head|tail|grep|egrep|fgrep|rg|diff|cmp|stat|file|test|'['|echo|printf|sort|uniq|jq|yq|git|gh|br|mkdir|touch|realpath|readlink|basename|dirname|du|md5sum|sha1sum|sha256sum|shasum|b2sum|cksum) return 0 ;;

+# _bdb_hd_tokenize <line> → _bdb_hd_tok[] (words keep their quotes; operators
+# are separate tokens, an fd number joins its redirect). Returns 1 when the
+# line cannot be read: open quote, trailing backslash, unquoted comment.
+_bdb_hd_tokenize() {
+  local s="${1:-}" n i=0 ch tok="" q="" have=0 op cand
+  n=${#s}

+  while (( i < n )); do
+    ch="${s:i:1}"
+    if [[ -n "$q" ]]; then
+      tok="$tok$ch"
+      if [[ "$q" == "'" ]]; then
+        [[ "$ch" == "'" ]] && q=""
+      elif [[ "$ch" == '\' ]]; then
+        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
+        i=$((i + 1)); tok="$tok${s:i:1}"
+      elif [[ "$ch" == '"' ]]; then
+        q=""
+      fi
+      i=$((i + 1)); continue
+    fi
+    case "$ch" in
+      "'"|'"') q="$ch"; tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      '\')
+        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
+        tok="$tok$ch${s:i+1:1}"; have=1; i=$((i + 2)) ;;
+      ' '|$'\t')
+        if (( have )); then _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"; tok=""; have=0; fi
+        i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      '#')
+        (( have )) || return 1
+        tok="$tok$ch"; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      ';'|'&'|'|'|'<'|'>'|'('|')')
+        op=""
+        for cand in '<<<' '<<-' '&>>' '<<' '>>' '>|' '&&' '||' '|&' '&>' '<>' '>&' '<&' ';;' ';' '&' '|' '<' '>' '(' ')'; do
+          if [[ "${s:i:${#cand}}" == "$cand" ]]; then op="$cand"; break; fi
+        done
+        i=$((i + ${#op}))
+        if [[ "$op" == '>&' || "$op" == '<&' ]]; then
+          while (( i < n )) && [[ "${s:i:1}" == [0-9-] ]]; do op="$op${s:i:1}"; i=$((i + 1)); done
+        fi
+        if (( have )); then
+          if [[ "$tok" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$op" == '<'* || "$op" == '>'* ]]; then
+            op="$tok$op"
+          else
+            _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
+          fi
+          tok=""; have=0
+        fi
+        _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$op" ;;
+      *) tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+    esac
+  done

+  (( have )) && _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"

+
+# _bdb_hd_unq_path <word> → _hd_up; returns 1 for a non-literal path (an
+# expansion, an escape, mixed quoting) or an empty one.
+_bdb_hd_unq_path() {
+  _hd_up=""
+  if [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_psq ]] || [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pdq ]]; then
+    _hd_up="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
+  elif [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pbare ]]; then
+    _hd_up="$1"
+  else
+    return 1
+  fi
+  [[ -n "$_hd_up" ]]

+
+# _bdb_hd_exec_dest <unquoted path> → 0 when a write there is executable
+# content (or cannot be judged).
+_bdb_hd_exec_dest() {
+  local p="${1:-}" d e b old_ifs
+  case "$p" in
+    *'*'*|*'?'*|*'['*|*'{'*|'~'|'~'[!/]*|'') return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  [[ "$p" == '~/'* ]] && p="${HOME:-}/${p#'~/'}"
+  b="${p##*/}"
+  [[ "$b" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ext ]] && return 0
+  [[ "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_sys || "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_rc ]] && return 0
+  [[ "$p" == /etc/* ]] && return 0
+  if [[ "$p" == /* ]]; then d="${p%/*}"; [[ -n "$d" ]] || d="/"
+  elif [[ "$p" == */* ]]; then d="${PWD:-.}/${p%/*}"
+  else d="${PWD:-.}"
+  fi

+    [[ -z "$e" || "$e" == "." ]] && e="${PWD:-.}"
+    [[ "$e" != "/" ]] && e="${e%/}"
+    if [[ "$d" == "$e" ]]; then IFS="$old_ifs"; return 0; fi
+  done

+# _bdb_hd_member <tokens…> → _hd_mcls (interpreter|nonexec|none) for one
+# pipeline member; write targets are appended to _hd_dests.
+_bdb_hd_member() {

+        *'<<<') return ;;
+        *'<<'|*'<<-') i=$((i + 1)); continue ;;
+        *'>&'[0-9]*|*'>&-'|*'<&'*) continue ;;
+        *'>'|*'>>'|*'>|'|*'>&'|'&>'|'&>>')

+          _bdb_hd_unq_path "$nxt" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }

+          _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up"

+        *) return ;;

+    t="${argv[i]}"
+    if [[ "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_exflag || "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_exlong ]]; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
+  done

+    cat)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do [[ "${argv[i]}" == "-" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; done ;;
+    tee)

+      done ;;
+    echo|printf)

+# _bdb_hd_ctx_bad <line> → 0 when a line before (or the header itself) leaves

+# pipeline: a later heredoc there is interpreter-class.
+_bdb_hd_ctx_bad() {

+# _bdb_hd_tokenize <line> → _bdb_hd_tok[] (words keep their quotes; operators

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# Issue #961 K-1 — Karpathy config schema (yq read + backward-compat defaults)
# =============================================================================
# Pins that `.loa.config.yaml.example` ships with the 7-key karpathy_principles
# block, and that the hook reads each key correctly with sensible defaults.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
    REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    EXAMPLE="$REPO_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml.example"
    [[ -f "$EXAMPLE" ]] || skip ".loa.config.yaml.example not found"
    command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not available"
}

@test "#961 K-1: .loa.config.yaml.example contains karpathy_principles block" {
    grep -q "^karpathy_principles:" "$EXAMPLE"
}

@test "#961 K-1: example exposes all 7 keys" {
    for key in surface_assumptions surgical_diff_warning diff_lines_per_task \
               simplicity_check max_abstraction_depth require_success_criteria enforce; do
        run yq eval ".karpathy_principles.${key}" "$EXAMPLE"
        [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
        [ "$output" != "null" ]
    done
}

@test "#961 K-1: hook defaults to 100 lines when threshold missing" {
    HOOK="$REPO_ROOT/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh"
    [[ -x "$HOOK" ]] || skip "hook not executable"

    local tmp
    tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
    export LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$tmp/cfg.yaml"
    export KARPATHY_TASK_STATE="$tmp/state.jsonl"
    export KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR="$tmp/traj"

    # Config with master switch on but threshold UNSET — should default to 100
    cat > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE" <<EOF
karpathy_principles:
  surgical_diff_warning: true
EOF

    # 50-line content: under default-100 threshold, no warn should fire
    local content
    content=$(yes line | head -50)
    local input
    input=$(jq -nc --arg c "$content" '{tool_name:"Write", tool_input:{file_path:"/tmp/x", content:$c}}')

    run bash -c "echo '$input' | '$HOOK' 2>&1"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    ! [[ "$output" == *"[karpathy-surgical-warn]"* ]]
}

content.text:
I found 7 defects in my scope. The derive and record-round bats suites mostly pass in a scratch copy at /tmp/rev-a once the two jq 1.6 problems in findings 1 and 2 are patched there. That run used a stub `verdict-derive.sh`, because the real one isn't in the frozen PR. The remaining derive failures (RCD-R1, R2, R3, R5) come from scripts outside the PR (session-start hook, preflight, golden-path, loa-status dependencies) and say nothing about this code.

### Findings

**1. `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378` — `$label` is a reserved jq keyword, so `derive` cannot compile on jq 1.6 (also used at lines 380 and 389).** The per-sprint jq program binds `--arg label` and refers to `$label`. jq 1.6 rejects this with "syntax error, unexpected label, expecting IDENT", which I reproduced on the jq 1.6 here; jq 1.7 accepts keyword binding names. Under `set -e`, `sj=$(...)` aborts every `derive`, so nearly all of the derive bats suite fails on jq 1.6. Worse, `write` and `mark` swallow derive failures (lines 174–175 and 541–542), so the caches are silently never derived and `/loa` never prints a drift line. jq 1.6 is the stock version on Ubuntu 22.04 and Debian 12. Renaming the variable (for example `$lbl`) fixes it. **Confidence: high** (reproduced); whether it matters depends on which jq versions the project supports.

**2. `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:226` (also line 223) — the empty-input fallback never fires on jq 1.6.** For a file without a trailer, `tl` and then `pj` are empty. jq 1.6 `jq -e 'type == "object"' <<<""` exits 0 when nothing is printed (verified), so `pj='{}'` is never assigned. `--argjson p ""` then fails and `fb_parse` prints nothing. The effects:
- `derive` aborts (exit 2) on any legacy feedback file.
- `record-round` on a legacy file exits 2, which I reproduced. Exit 2 means "usage" and does not halt the run.
- Line 223 has the same hole for `vj` if `verdict-derive.sh` prints nothing.

Guarding with `[[ -n "$pj" ]] && …` fixes it. **Confidence: medium** (jq 1.6 specific).

**3. `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:527` — a trip can return 3 instead of 10, and the SKILL then keeps the run going (with `head/.claude/skills/run-mode/SKILL.md:110`).** `record-round` writes `OPEN` and history to the breaker first, then sets `HALTED` in `state.json`. If that second write fails (corrupt `state.json`, lock timeout, missing directory) it returns 3 and never prints `TRIPPED:`. SKILL.md line 110 says "exit 10, HALT; else continue loop", so exit 3, and exit 2 from finding 2, both continue the loop past a tripped breaker. I reproduced it: three identical rounds against a corrupt `state.json` give rc 3 with the breaker `OPEN`, and the next round is rc 3 again. The trip should still exit 10 (or the halt write should come first), and the SKILL should halt on any non-zero exit other than 0. **Confidence: high.**

**4. `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:403` — the breaker is recomputed over the wrong sprint, and legacy feedback can falsely trip it.** The active sprint is the first sprint whose derived state isn't `complete`, ignoring its ledger status. A sprint with legacy (no-trailer) feedback can never derive `complete` (RCD-3 confirms this), so it stays the active sprint for the rest of the cycle. In `recompute`:
- every legacy file counts as a non-approved round;
- every legacy file without a Findings/Issues/Changes Required section hashes to md5 of empty input;
- legacy counts are all `null`, so they also count as no-progress.

I reproduced it: an old sprint with ledger status `completed` and three legacy files ("All good", "APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO", "Looks good now") made `derive --write` open the breaker (`same_issue` 3, source derive) and set the run `HALTED` while sprint-102 was the one being worked on. `derive` runs on every `write` and `mark`, so this fires without anyone asking. **Confidence: medium-high.**

**5. `head/.claude/skills/run-mode/resources/halt-resume.md:81` — the `--reset-ice` recipe doesn't clear the new `triggers.no_progress.last_counts`.** `record-round` now stores `last_counts` (state-schemas.md documents it), but the reset leaves it in place. The first round after a reset with unchanged counts therefore records `no_progress 1/5` instead of 0; I reproduced this. So the reset isn't a full reset, contrary to the doc's "rounds before it no longer count". **Confidence: medium.**

**6. `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:496` — `record-round` turns a breaker without an object `.triggers` into a fresh CLOSED skeleton, dropping `state: OPEN`.** Example: `{"state":"OPEN","history":[…]}`. I reproduced it: the result is `CLOSED`, history `[]`, rc 0. That fails open, and it doesn't match `derive`'s `merge_breaker` (line 295), which keeps `.state`. Relatedly, at line 411 an unparseable breaker becomes `null`, so `derive --json` (used by `/loa` and run-resume step 0a) reports the breaker `CLOSED` and the run not `HALTED`. **Confidence: medium** (needs a malformed or hand-edited breaker file).

**7. `head/tests/unit/run-checkpoint-record-round.bats:105` — RCR-5 claims to test trigger order but cannot.** Each sub-case builds a fresh breaker where only one trigger can fire, so reordering the `if/elif` chain at lines 507–516 would still pass. The order in the test name (cycle limit, no-progress, timeout) also differs from the documented order (same_issue, no_progress, cycle_count, timeout), and nothing tests same_issue taking precedence. **Confidence: medium.**

### Minor doc mismatch
`head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:50` documents derive's exits as 0, 4 and 2. In fact `--write` returns 3 on breaker or state write failure (lines 456 and 459). Failed jq calls under `set -e` exit with jq's own code (2, 3 or 5), and 2 collides with "usage". **Confidence: high, low impact.**

# branches mandate, respectively, the literals `.run/` (from \.run/…\.sh),

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Path fragments (ERE; substring match also covers absolute / $PWD-prefixed forms).
_sz_pc="[^[:space:]'\";&|#]"                              # one path character
_sz_sh="\\.run/${_sz_pc}*\\.sh"                          # a .sh file anywhere under .run/
_sz_root="(\\.run/cron\\.d|grimoires/loa/skills)"        # protected directory roots
_sz_tgt="(${_sz_sh}|${_sz_root}(/${_sz_pc}*)?)"          # a protected target (file OR dir[/desc])
_sz_file="(${_sz_sh}|${_sz_root}/${_sz_pc}*)"            # a protected descendant FILE
_sz_b="([[:space:]]|['\"]|[;&|#]|\$)"                    # right token boundary (NOT '/')
_sz_end="([[:space:]]+--?[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9-]*)*[[:space:]]*([;&|#]|\$)"  # end-of-stmt; allows trailing option flags (GNU options-after-operands)
_sz_pre="${_sz_pc}*"                                     # optional leading path prefix (./, abs, $PWD/, repo-root)

if [[ "$command" == *".run/"* || "$command" == *"grimoires/loa/skills"* ]] \
   && _match "(${_sz_sh}|\\.run/cron\\.d|grimoires/loa/skills)"; then

      export LOA_SZ_EXEC_WRITE_BYPASS_WARNED=1

      _sz_cmd=$(printf '%s' "$command" | "$_sz_redactor" 2>/dev/null) || _sz_cmd="[REDACTOR-FAILED]"
      [[ ${#_sz_cmd} -gt 2048 ]] && _sz_cmd="${_sz_cmd:0:2048}[...TRUNCATED]"
      mkdir -p "${LOA_REPO_ROOT:-.}/.run" 2>/dev/null || true

                          and (.reason|type=="string") and ((.reason|length)>0)
                          and (.expires_at|type=="string")
                          and (.expires_at|test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z$")))
                        | .expires_at' "$_c2_auth_file" 2>/dev/null)" || _c2_row=""
      if [[ -n "$_c2_row" ]]; then

Feedback files end with a `LOA-VERDICT` trailer; `verdict-derive.sh` enforces prose/trailer consistency and the one-way rule (critical+high > 0 ⇒ CHANGES_REQUIRED; zero never forces approval). Fence inventory and accepted bypasses: `.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md`.
